texts.webp: On the next day, the multitude that stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other boat there, except the one in which his disciples had embarked, and that Jesus hadn’t entered with his disciples into the boat, but his disciples had gone away alone.
texts.bsb: The next day, the crowd that had remained on the other side of the sea realized that only one boat had been there, and that Jesus had not boarded it with His disciples, but they had gone away alone.
texts.asv: On the morrow the multitude that stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other boat there, save one, and that Jesus entered not with his disciples into the boat, but that his disciples went away alone

texts.webp: However, boats from Tiberias came near to the place where they ate the bread after the Lord had given thanks.
texts.bsb: However, some boats from Tiberias landed near the place where the people had eaten the bread after the Lord had given thanks.
texts.asv: (howbeit there came boats from Tiberias nigh unto the place where they ate the bread after the Lord had given thanks):

texts.webp: When the multitude therefore saw that Jesus wasn’t there, nor his disciples, they themselves got into the boats and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.
texts.bsb: So when the crowd saw that neither Jesus nor His disciples were there, they got into the boats and went to Capernaum to look for Him.
texts.asv: when the multitude therefore saw that Jesus was not there, neither his disciples, they themselves got into the boats, and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.

texts.webp: When they found him on the other side of the sea, they asked him, “Rabbi, when did you come here?”
texts.bsb: When they found Him on the other side of the sea, they asked Him, “Rabbi, when did You get here?”
texts.asv: And when they found him on the other side of the sea, they said unto him, Rabbi, when camest thou hither?

texts.webp: Jesus answered them, “Most certainly I tell you, you seek me, not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled.
texts.bsb: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it is not because you saw these signs that you are looking for Me, but because you ate the loaves and had your fill.
texts.asv: Jesus answered them and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Ye seek me, not because ye saw signs, but because ye ate of the loaves, and were filled.

texts.webp: Don’t work for the food which perishes, but for the food which remains to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give to you. For God the Father has sealed him.”
texts.bsb: Do not work for food that perishes, but for food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For on Him God the Father has placed His seal of approval.”
texts.asv: Work not for the food which perisheth, but for the food which abideth unto eternal life, which the Son of man shall give unto you: for him the Father, even God, hath sealed.

texts.webp: They said therefore to him, “What must we do, that we may work the works of God?”
texts.bsb: Then they inquired, “What must we do to perform the works of God?”
texts.asv: They said therefore unto him, What must we do, that we may work the works of God?

texts.webp: Jesus answered them, “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.”
texts.bsb: Jesus replied, “The work of God is this: to believe in the One He has sent.”
texts.asv: Jesus answered and said unto them, This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent.

texts.webp: They said therefore to him, “What then do you do for a sign, that we may see and believe you? What work do you do?
texts.bsb: So they asked Him, “What sign then will You perform, so that we may see it and believe You? What will You do?
texts.asv: They said therefore unto him, What then doest thou for a sign, that we may see, and believe thee? what workest thou?

texts.webp: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness. As it is written, ‘He gave them bread out of heaven to eat.’”
texts.bsb: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, as it is written: ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’ ”
texts.asv: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness; as it is written, He gave them bread out of heaven to eat.

texts.webp: Jesus therefore said to them, “Most certainly, I tell you, it wasn’t Moses who gave you the bread out of heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread out of heaven.
texts.bsb: Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven, but it is My Father who gives you the true bread from heaven.
texts.asv: Jesus therefore said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, It was not Moses that gave you the bread out of heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread out of heaven.

texts.webp: For the bread of God is that which comes down out of heaven and gives life to the world.”
texts.bsb: For the bread of God is He who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.”
texts.asv: For the bread of God is that which cometh down out of heaven, and giveth life unto the world.

texts.webp: They said therefore to him, “Lord, always give us this bread.”
texts.bsb: “Sir,” they said, “give us this bread at all times.”
texts.asv: They said therefore unto him, Lord, evermore give us this bread.

texts.webp: Jesus said to them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.
texts.bsb: Jesus answered, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to Me will never hunger, and whoever believes in Me will never thirst.
texts.asv: Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall not hunger, and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.

texts.webp: But I told you that you have seen me, and yet you don’t believe.
texts.bsb: But as I stated, you have seen Me and still you do not believe.
texts.asv: But I said unto you, that ye have seen me, and yet believe not.

texts.webp: All those whom the Father gives me will come to me. He who comes to me I will in no way throw out.
texts.bsb: Everyone the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will never drive away.
texts.asv: All that which the Father giveth me shall come unto me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out.

texts.webp: For I have come down from heaven, not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me.
texts.bsb: For I have come down from heaven, not to do My own will, but to do the will of Him who sent Me.
texts.asv: For I am come down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me.

texts.webp: This is the will of my Father who sent me, that of all he has given to me I should lose nothing, but should raise him up at the last day.
texts.bsb: And this is the will of Him who sent Me, that I shall lose none of those He has given Me, but raise them up at the last day.
texts.asv: And this is the will of him that sent me, that of all that which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up at the last day.

texts.webp: This is the will of the one who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.”
texts.bsb: For it is My Father’s will that everyone who looks to the Son and believes in Him shall have eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.”
texts.asv: For this is the will of my Father, that every one that beholdeth the Son, and believeth on him, should have eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.

texts.webp: The Jews therefore murmured concerning him, because he said, “I am the bread which came down out of heaven.”
texts.bsb: At this, the Jews began to grumble about Jesus because He had said, “I am the bread that came down from heaven.”
texts.asv: The Jews therefore murmured concerning him, because he said, I am the bread which came down out of heaven.

texts.webp: They said, “Isn’t this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then does he say, ‘I have come down out of heaven’?”
texts.bsb: They were asking, “Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then can He say, ‘I have come down from heaven’?”
texts.asv: And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how doth he now say, I am come down out of heaven?

texts.webp: Therefore Jesus answered them, “Don’t murmur among yourselves.
texts.bsb: “Stop grumbling among yourselves,” Jesus replied.
texts.asv: Jesus answered and said unto them, Murmur not among yourselves.

texts.webp: No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him; and I will raise him up in the last day.
texts.bsb: “No one can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him, and I will raise him up at the last day.
texts.asv: No man can come to me, except the Father that sent me draw him: and I will raise him up in the last day.

texts.webp: It is written in the prophets, ‘They will all be taught by God.’ Therefore everyone who hears from the Father and has learned, comes to me.
texts.bsb: It is written in the Prophets: ‘And they will all be taught by God.’ Everyone who has heard the Father and learned from Him comes to Me —
texts.asv: It is written in the prophets, And they shall all be taught of God. Every one that hath heard from the Father, and hath learned, cometh unto me.

texts.webp: Not that anyone has seen the Father, except he who is from God. He has seen the Father.
texts.bsb: not that anyone has seen the Father except the One who is from God; only He has seen the Father.
texts.asv: Not that any man hath seen the Father, save he that is from God, he hath seen the Father.

texts.webp: Most certainly, I tell you, he who believes in me has eternal life.
texts.bsb: Truly, truly, I tell you, he who believes has eternal life.
texts.asv: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth hath eternal life.

texts.webp: I am the bread of life.
texts.bsb: I am the bread of life.
texts.asv: I am the bread of life.

texts.webp: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness and they died.
texts.bsb: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, yet they died.
texts.asv: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died.

texts.webp: This is the bread which comes down out of heaven, that anyone may eat of it and not die.
texts.bsb: This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and not die.
texts.asv: This is the bread which cometh down out of heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die.

texts.webp: I am the living bread which came down out of heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. Yes, the bread which I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.”
texts.bsb: I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. And this bread, which I will give for the life of the world, is My flesh.”
texts.asv: I am the living bread which came down out of heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: yea and the bread which I will give is my flesh, for the life of the world.

texts.webp: The Jews therefore contended with one another, saying, “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?”
texts.bsb: At this, the Jews began to argue among themselves, “How can this man give us His flesh to eat?”
texts.asv: The Jews therefore strove one with another, saying, How can this man give us his flesh to eat?

texts.webp: Jesus therefore said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you don’t have life in yourselves.
texts.bsb: So Jesus said to them, “Truly, truly, I tell you, unless you eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man, you have no life in you.
texts.asv: Jesus therefore said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of man and drink his blood, ye have not life in yourselves.

texts.webp: He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.
texts.bsb: Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day.
texts.asv: He that eateth my flesh and drinketh my blood hath eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day.

texts.webp: For my flesh is food indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.
texts.bsb: For My flesh is real food, and My blood is real drink.
texts.asv: For my flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed.

texts.webp: He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood lives in me, and I in him.
texts.bsb: Whoever eats My flesh and drinks My blood remains in Me, and I in him.
texts.asv: He that eateth my flesh and drinketh my blood abideth in me, and I in him.

texts.webp: As the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, so he who feeds on me will also live because of me.
texts.bsb: Just as the living Father sent Me and I live because of the Father, so also the one who feeds on Me will live because of Me.
texts.asv: As the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father; so he that eateth me, he also shall live because of me.

texts.webp: This is the bread which came down out of heaven—not as our fathers ate the manna and died. He who eats this bread will live forever.”
texts.bsb: This is the bread that came down from heaven. Unlike your fathers, who ate the manna and died, the one who eats this bread will live forever.”
texts.asv: This is the bread which came down out of heaven: not as the fathers ate, and died; he that eateth this bread shall live for ever.

texts.webp: He said these things in the synagogue, as he taught in Capernaum.
texts.bsb: Jesus said this while teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum.
texts.asv: These things said he in the synagogue, as he taught in Capernaum.

texts.webp: Therefore many of his disciples, when they heard this, said, “This is a hard saying! Who can listen to it?”
texts.bsb: On hearing it, many of His disciples said, “This is a difficult teaching. Who can accept it?”
texts.asv: Many therefore of his disciples, when they heard this, said, This is a hard saying; who can hear it?

texts.webp: But Jesus knowing in himself that his disciples murmured at this, said to them, “Does this cause you to stumble?
texts.bsb: Aware that His disciples were grumbling about this teaching, Jesus asked them, “Does this offend you?
texts.asv: But Jesus knowing in himself that his disciples murmured at this, said unto them, Doth this cause you to stumble?

texts.webp: Then what if you would see the Son of Man ascending to where he was before?
texts.bsb: Then what will happen if you see the Son of Man ascend to where He was before?
texts.asv: What then if ye should behold the Son of man ascending where he was before?

texts.webp: It is the spirit who gives life. The flesh profits nothing. The words that I speak to you are spirit, and are life.
texts.bsb: The Spirit gives life; the flesh profits nothing. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and they are life.
texts.asv: It is the spirit that giveth life; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I have spoken unto you are spirit, and are life.

texts.webp: But there are some of you who don’t believe.” For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were who didn’t believe, and who it was who would betray him.
texts.bsb: However, there are some of you who do not believe.” (For Jesus had known from the beginning which of them did not believe and who would betray Him.)
texts.asv: But there are some of you that believe not. For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were that believed not, and who it was that should betray him.

texts.webp: He said, “For this cause I have said to you that no one can come to me, unless it is given to him by my Father.”
texts.bsb: Then Jesus said, “This is why I told you that no one can come to Me unless the Father has granted it to him.”
texts.asv: And he said, For this cause have I said unto you, that no man can come unto me, except it be given unto him of the Father.

texts.webp: At this, many of his disciples went back and walked no more with him.
texts.bsb: From that time on many of His disciples turned back and no longer walked with Him.
texts.asv: Upon this many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him.

texts.webp: Jesus said therefore to the twelve, “You don’t also want to go away, do you?”
texts.bsb: So Jesus asked the Twelve, “Do you want to leave too?”
texts.asv: Jesus said therefore unto the twelve, Would ye also go away?

texts.webp: Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.
texts.bsb: Simon Peter replied, “Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.
texts.asv: Simon Peter answered him, Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.

texts.webp: We have come to believe and know that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
texts.bsb: We believe and know that You are the Holy One of God. ”
texts.asv: And we have believed and know that thou art the Holy One of God.

texts.webp: Jesus answered them, “Didn’t I choose you, the twelve, and one of you is a devil?”
texts.bsb: Jesus answered them, “Have I not chosen you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil!”
texts.asv: Jesus answered them, Did not I choose you the twelve, and one of you is a devil?

texts.webp: Now he spoke of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, for it was he who would betray him, being one of the twelve.
texts.bsb: He was speaking about Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot. For although Judas was one of the Twelve, he was later to betray Jesus.
texts.asv: Now he spake of Judas the son of Simon Iscariot, for he it was that should betray him, being one of the twelve.

texts.webp: After these things, Jesus was walking in Galilee, for he wouldn’t walk in Judea, because the Jews sought to kill him.
texts.bsb: After this, Jesus traveled throughout Galilee. He did not want to travel in Judea, because the Jews there were trying to kill Him.
texts.asv: And after these things Jesus walked in Galilee: for he would not walk in Judæa, because the Jews sought to kill him.

texts.webp: Now the feast of the Jews, the Feast of Booths, was at hand.
texts.bsb: However, the Jewish Feast of Tabernacles was near.
texts.asv: Now the feast of the Jews, the feast of tabernacles, was at hand.

texts.webp: His brothers therefore said to him, “Depart from here and go into Judea, that your disciples also may see your works which you do.
texts.bsb: So Jesus’ brothers said to Him, “Leave here and go to Judea, so that Your disciples there may see the works You are doing.
texts.asv: His brethren therefore said unto him, Depart hence, and go into Judæa, that thy disciples also may behold thy works which thou doest.

texts.webp: For no one does anything in secret while he seeks to be known openly. If you do these things, reveal yourself to the world.”
texts.bsb: For no one who wants to be known publicly acts in secret. Since You are doing these things, show Yourself to the world.”
texts.asv: For no man doeth anything in secret, and himself seeketh to be known openly. If thou doest these things, manifest thyself to the world.

texts.webp: For even his brothers didn’t believe in him.
texts.bsb: For even His own brothers did not believe in Him.
texts.asv: For even his brethren did not believe on him.

texts.webp: Jesus therefore said to them, “My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready.
texts.bsb: Therefore Jesus told them, “Although your time is always at hand, My time has not yet come.
texts.asv: Jesus therefore saith unto them, My time is not yet come; but your time is always ready.

texts.webp: The world can’t hate you, but it hates me, because I testify about it, that its works are evil.
texts.bsb: The world cannot hate you, but it hates Me, because I testify that its works are evil.
texts.asv: The world cannot hate you; but me it hateth, because I testify of it, that its works are evil.

texts.webp: You go up to the feast. I am not yet going up to this feast, because my time is not yet fulfilled.”
texts.bsb: Go up to the feast on your own. I am not going up to this feast, because My time has not yet come.”
texts.asv: Go ye up unto the feast: I go not up unto this feast; because my time is not yet fulfilled.

texts.webp: Having said these things to them, he stayed in Galilee.
texts.bsb: Having said this, Jesus remained in Galilee.
texts.asv: And having said these things unto them, he abode still in Galilee.

texts.webp: But when his brothers had gone up to the feast, then he also went up, not publicly, but as it were in secret.
texts.bsb: But after His brothers had gone up to the feast, He also went — not publicly, but in secret.
texts.asv: But when his brethren were gone up unto the feast, then went he also up, not publicly, but as it were in secret.

texts.webp: The Jews therefore sought him at the feast, and said, “Where is he?”
texts.bsb: So the Jews were looking for Him at the feast and asking, “Where is He?”
texts.asv: The Jews therefore sought him at the feast, and said, Where is he?

texts.webp: There was much murmuring among the multitudes concerning him. Some said, “He is a good man.” Others said, “Not so, but he leads the multitude astray.”
texts.bsb: Many in the crowds were whispering about Him. Some said, “He is a good man.”
texts.asv: And there was much murmuring among the multitudes concerning him: some said, He is a good man; others said, Not so, but he leadeth the multitude astray.

texts.webp: Yet no one spoke openly of him for fear of the Jews.
texts.bsb: Yet no one would speak publicly about Him for fear of the Jews.
texts.asv: Yet no man spake openly of him for fear of the Jews.

texts.webp: But when it was now the middle of the feast, Jesus went up into the temple and taught.
texts.bsb: About halfway through the feast, Jesus went up to the temple courts and began to teach.
texts.asv: But when it was now the midst of the feast Jesus went up into the temple, and taught.

texts.webp: The Jews therefore marveled, saying, “How does this man know letters, having never been educated?”
texts.bsb: The Jews were amazed and asked, “How did this man attain such learning without having studied?”
texts.asv: The Jews therefore marvelled, saying, How knoweth this man letters, having never learned?

texts.webp: Jesus therefore answered them, “My teaching is not mine, but his who sent me.
texts.bsb: “My teaching is not My own,” Jesus replied. “It comes from Him who sent Me.
texts.asv: Jesus therefore answered them, and said, My teaching is not mine, but his that sent me.

texts.webp: If anyone desires to do his will, he will know about the teaching, whether it is from God or if I am speaking from myself.
texts.bsb: If anyone desires to do His will, he will know whether My teaching is from God or whether I speak on My own.
texts.asv: If any man willeth to do his will, he shall know of the teaching, whether it is of God, or whether I speak from myself.

texts.webp: He who speaks from himself seeks his own glory, but he who seeks the glory of him who sent him is true, and no unrighteousness is in him.
texts.bsb: He who speaks on his own authority seeks his own glory, but He who seeks the glory of the One who sent Him is a man of truth; in Him there is no falsehood.
texts.asv: He that speaketh from himself seeketh his own glory: but he that seeketh the glory of him that sent him, the same is true, and no unrighteousness is in him.

texts.webp: Didn’t Moses give you the law, and yet none of you keeps the law? Why do you seek to kill me?”
texts.bsb: Has not Moses given you the law? Yet not one of you keeps it. Why are you trying to kill Me?”
texts.asv: Did not Moses give you the law, and yet none of you doeth the law? Why seek ye to kill me?

texts.webp: The multitude answered, “You have a demon! Who seeks to kill you?”
texts.bsb: “You have a demon,” the crowd replied. “Who is trying to kill You?”
texts.asv: The multitude answered, Thou hast a demon: who seeketh to kill thee?

texts.webp: Jesus answered them, “I did one work and you all marvel because of it.
texts.bsb: Jesus answered them, “I did one miracle, and you are all amazed.
texts.asv: Jesus answered and said unto them, I did one work, and ye all marvel because thereof.

texts.webp: Moses has given you circumcision (not that it is of Moses, but of the fathers), and on the Sabbath you circumcise a boy.
texts.bsb: But because Moses gave you circumcision, you circumcise a boy on the Sabbath (not that it is from Moses, but from the patriarchs.)
texts.asv: Moses hath given you circumcision (not that it is of Moses, but of the fathers); and on the sabbath ye circumcise a man.

texts.webp: If a boy receives circumcision on the Sabbath, that the law of Moses may not be broken, are you angry with me because I made a man completely healthy on the Sabbath?
texts.bsb: If a boy can be circumcised on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses will not be broken, why are you angry with Me for making the whole man well on the Sabbath?
texts.asv: If a man receiveth circumcision on the sabbath, that the law of Moses may not be broken; are ye wroth with me, because I made a man every whit whole on the sabbath?

texts.webp: Don’t judge according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment.”
texts.bsb: Stop judging by outward appearances, and start judging justly.”
texts.asv: Judge not according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment.

texts.webp: Therefore some of them of Jerusalem said, “Isn’t this he whom they seek to kill?
texts.bsb: Then some of the people of Jerusalem began to say, “Isn’t this the man they are trying to kill?
texts.asv: Some therefore of them of Jerusalem said, Is not this he whom they seek to kill?

texts.webp: Behold, he speaks openly, and they say nothing to him. Can it be that the rulers indeed know that this is truly the Christ?
texts.bsb: Yet here He is, speaking publicly, and they are not saying anything to Him. Have the rulers truly recognized that this is the Christ?
texts.asv: And lo, he speaketh openly, and they say nothing unto him. Can it be that the rulers indeed know that this is the Christ?

texts.webp: However, we know where this man comes from, but when the Christ comes, no one will know where he comes from.”
texts.bsb: But we know where this man is from. When the Christ comes, no one will know where He is from.”
texts.asv: Howbeit we know this man whence he is: but when the Christ cometh, no one knoweth whence he is.

texts.webp: Jesus therefore cried out in the temple, teaching and saying, “You both know me, and know where I am from. I have not come of myself, but he who sent me is true, whom you don’t know.
texts.bsb: Then Jesus, still teaching in the temple courts, cried out, “You know Me, and you know where I am from. I have not come of My own accord, but He who sent Me is true. You do not know Him,
texts.asv: Jesus therefore cried in the temple, teaching and saying, Ye both know me, and know whence I am; and I am not come of myself, but he that sent me is true, whom ye know not.

texts.webp: I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me.”
texts.bsb: but I know Him, because I am from Him and He sent Me.”
texts.asv: I know him; because I am from him, and he sent me.

texts.webp: They sought therefore to take him; but no one laid a hand on him, because his hour had not yet come.
texts.bsb: So they tried to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him, because His hour had not yet come.
texts.asv: They sought therefore to take him: and no man laid his hand on him, because his hour was not yet come.

texts.webp: But of the multitude, many believed in him. They said, “When the Christ comes, he won’t do more signs than those which this man has done, will he?”
texts.bsb: Many in the crowd, however, believed in Him and said, “When the Christ comes, will He perform more signs than this man?”
texts.asv: But of the multitude many believed on him; and they said, When the Christ shall come, will he do more signs than those which this man hath done?

texts.webp: The Pharisees heard the multitude murmuring these things concerning him, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to arrest him.
texts.bsb: When the Pharisees heard the crowd whispering these things about Jesus, they and the chief priests sent officers to arrest Him.
texts.asv: The Pharisees heard the multitude murmuring these things concerning him; and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to take him.

texts.webp: Then Jesus said, “I will be with you a little while longer, then I go to him who sent me.
texts.bsb: So Jesus said, “I am with you only a little while longer, and then I am going to the One who sent Me.
texts.asv: Jesus therefore said, Yet a little while am I with you, and I go unto him that sent me.

texts.webp: You will seek me and won’t find me. You can’t come where I am.”
texts.bsb: You will look for Me, but you will not find Me; and where I am, you cannot come.”
texts.asv: Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me: and where I am, ye cannot come.

texts.webp: The Jews therefore said among themselves, “Where will this man go that we won’t find him? Will he go to the Dispersion among the Greeks and teach the Greeks?
texts.bsb: At this, the Jews said to one another, “Where does He intend to go that we will not find Him? Will He go where the Jews are dispersed among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?
texts.asv: The Jews therefore said among themselves, Whither will this man go that we shall not find him? will he go unto the Dispersion among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?

texts.webp: What is this word that he said, ‘You will seek me, and won’t find me;’ and ‘Where I am, you can’t come’?”
texts.bsb: What does He mean by saying, ‘You will look for Me, but you will not find Me,’ and, ‘Where I am, you cannot come’?”
texts.asv: What is this word that he said, Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me; and where I am, ye cannot come?

texts.webp: Now on the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink!
texts.bsb: On the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood up and called out in a loud voice, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink.
texts.asv: Now on the last day, the great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me and drink.

texts.webp: He who believes in me, as the Scripture has said, from within him will flow rivers of living water.”
texts.bsb: Whoever believes in Me, as the Scripture has said: ‘Streams of living water will flow from within him.’”
texts.asv: He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, from within him shall flow rivers of living water.

texts.webp: But he said this about the Spirit, which those believing in him were to receive. For the Holy Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus wasn’t yet glorified.
texts.bsb: He was speaking about the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were later to receive. For the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
texts.asv: But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believed on him were to receive: for the Spirit was not yet given; because Jesus was not yet glorified.

texts.webp: Many of the multitude therefore, when they heard these words, said, “This is truly the prophet.”
texts.bsb: On hearing these words, some of the people said, “This is truly the Prophet.”
texts.asv: Some of the multitude therefore, when they heard these words, said, This is of a truth the prophet.

texts.webp: Others said, “This is the Christ.” But some said, “What, does the Christ come out of Galilee?
texts.bsb: Others declared, “This is the Christ.”
texts.asv: Others said, This is the Christ. But some said, What, doth the Christ come out of Galilee?

texts.webp: Hasn’t the Scripture said that the Christ comes of the offspring of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?”
texts.bsb: Doesn’t the Scripture say that the Christ will come from the line of David and from Bethlehem, the village where David lived? ”
texts.asv: Hath not the scripture said that the Christ cometh of the seed of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?

texts.webp: So a division arose in the multitude because of him.
texts.bsb: So there was division in the crowd because of Jesus.
texts.asv: So there arose a division in the multitude because of him.

texts.webp: Some of them would have arrested him, but no one laid hands on him.
texts.bsb: Some of them wanted to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him.
texts.asv: And some of them would have taken him; but no man laid hands on him.

texts.webp: The officers therefore came to the chief priests and Pharisees; and they said to them, “Why didn’t you bring him?”
texts.bsb: Then the officers returned to the chief priests and Pharisees, who asked them, “Why didn’t you bring Him in?”
texts.asv: The officers therefore came to the chief priests and Pharisees; and they said unto them, Why did ye not bring him?

texts.webp: The officers answered, “No man ever spoke like this man!”
texts.bsb: “Never has anyone spoken like this man!” the officers answered.
texts.asv: The officers answered, Never man so spake.

texts.webp: The Pharisees therefore answered them, “You aren’t also led astray, are you?
texts.bsb: “Have you also been deceived?” replied the Pharisees.
texts.asv: The Pharisees therefore answered them, Are ye also led astray?

texts.webp: Have any of the rulers or any of the Pharisees believed in him?
texts.bsb: “Have any of the rulers or Pharisees believed in Him?
texts.asv: Hath any of the rulers believed on him, or of the Pharisees?

texts.webp: But this multitude that doesn’t know the law is cursed.”
texts.bsb: But this crowd that does not know the law— they are under a curse.”
texts.asv: But this multitude that knoweth not the law are accursed.

texts.webp: Nicodemus (he who came to him by night, being one of them) said to them,
texts.bsb: Nicodemus, who had gone to Jesus earlier and who himself was one of them, asked,
texts.asv: Nicodemus saith unto them (he that came to him before, being one of them),

texts.webp: “Does our law judge a man unless it first hears from him personally and knows what he does?”
texts.bsb: “Does our law convict a man without first hearing from him to determine what he has done?”
texts.asv: Doth our law judge a man, except it first hear from himself and know what he doeth?

texts.webp: They answered him, “Are you also from Galilee? Search and see that no prophet has arisen out of Galilee.”
texts.bsb: “Aren’t you also from Galilee?” they replied. “Look into it, and you will see that no prophet comes out of Galilee.”
texts.asv: They answered and said unto him, Art thou also of Galilee? Search, and see that out of Galilee ariseth no prophet.

texts.webp: Everyone went to his own house,
texts.bsb: Then each went to his own home.
texts.asv: [And they went every man unto his own house:

texts.webp: but Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
texts.bsb: But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
texts.asv: but Jesus went unto the mount of Olives.

texts.webp: Now very early in the morning, he came again into the temple, and all the people came to him. He sat down and taught them.
texts.bsb: Early in the morning He went back into the temple courts. All the people came to Him, and He sat down to teach them.
texts.asv: And early in the morning he came again into the temple, and all the people came unto him; and he sat down, and taught them.

texts.webp: The scribes and the Pharisees brought a woman taken in adultery. Having set her in the middle,
texts.bsb: The scribes and Pharisees, however, brought to Him a woman caught in adultery. They made her stand before them
texts.asv: And the scribes and the Pharisees bring a woman taken in adultery; and having set her in the midst,

texts.webp: they told him, “Teacher, we found this woman in adultery, in the very act.
texts.bsb: and said, “Teacher, this woman was caught in the act of adultery.
texts.asv: they say unto him, Teacher, this woman hath been taken in adultery, in the very act.

texts.webp: Now in our law, Moses commanded us to stone such women. What then do you say about her?”
texts.bsb: In the Law Moses commanded us to stone such a woman. So what do You say?”
texts.asv: Now in the law Moses commanded us to stone such: what then sayest thou of her?

texts.webp: They said this testing him, that they might have something to accuse him of.
texts.bsb: They said this to test Him, in order to have a basis for accusing Him. But Jesus bent down and began to write on the ground with His finger.
texts.asv: And this they said, trying him, that they might have whereof to accuse him. But Jesus stooped down, and with his finger wrote on the ground.

texts.webp: But when they continued asking him, he looked up and said to them, “He who is without sin among you, let him throw the first stone at her.”
texts.bsb: When they continued to question Him, He straightened up and said to them, “Let him who is without sin among you be the first to cast a stone at her.”
texts.asv: But when they continued asking him, he lifted up himself, and said unto them, He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.

texts.webp: Again he stooped down and wrote on the ground with his finger.
texts.bsb: And again He bent down and wrote on the ground.
texts.asv: And again he stooped down, and with his finger wrote on the ground.

texts.webp: They, when they heard it, being convicted by their conscience, went out one by one, beginning from the oldest, even to the last. Jesus was left alone with the woman where she was, in the middle.
texts.bsb: When they heard this, they began to go away one by one, beginning with the older ones, until only Jesus was left, with the woman standing there.
texts.asv: And they, when they heard it, went out one by one, beginning from the eldest, even unto the last: and Jesus was left alone, and the woman, where she was, in the midst.

texts.webp: Jesus, standing up, saw her and said, “Woman, where are your accusers? Did no one condemn you?”
texts.bsb: Then Jesus straightened up and asked her, “Woman, where are your accusers? Has no one condemned you?”
texts.asv: And Jesus lifted up himself, and said unto her, Woman, where are they? did no man condemn thee?

texts.webp: She said, “No one, Lord.”
texts.bsb: “No one, Lord,” she answered.
texts.asv: And she said, No man, Lord. And Jesus said, Neither do I condemn thee: go thy way; from henceforth sin no more.]

texts.webp: Again, therefore, Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. He who follows me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”
texts.bsb: Once again, Jesus spoke to the people and said, “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows Me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”
texts.asv: Again therefore Jesus spake unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in the darkness, but shall have the light of life.

texts.webp: The Pharisees therefore said to him, “You testify about yourself. Your testimony is not valid.”
texts.bsb: So the Pharisees said to Him, “You are testifying about Yourself; Your testimony is not valid.”
texts.asv: The Pharisees therefore said unto him, Thou bearest witness of thyself; thy witness is not true.

texts.webp: Jesus answered them, “Even if I testify about myself, my testimony is true, for I know where I came from, and where I am going; but you don’t know where I came from, or where I am going.
texts.bsb: Jesus replied, “Even if I testify about Myself, My testimony is valid, because I know where I came from and where I am going. But you do not know where I came from or where I am going.
texts.asv: Jesus answered and said unto them, Even if I bear witness of myself, my witness is true; for I know whence I came, and whither I go; but ye know not whence I come, or whither I go.

texts.webp: You judge according to the flesh. I judge no one.
texts.bsb: You judge according to the flesh; I judge no one.
texts.asv: Ye judge after the flesh; I judge no man.

texts.webp: Even if I do judge, my judgment is true, for I am not alone, but I am with the Father who sent me.
texts.bsb: But even if I do judge, My judgment is true, because I am not alone; I am with the Father who sent Me.
texts.asv: Yea and if I judge, my judgment is true; for I am not alone, but I and the Father that sent me.

texts.webp: It’s also written in your law that the testimony of two people is valid.
texts.bsb: Even in your own Law it is written that the testimony of two men is valid.
texts.asv: Yea and in your law it is written, that the witness of two men is true.

texts.webp: I am one who testifies about myself, and the Father who sent me testifies about me.”
texts.bsb: I am One who testifies about Myself, and the Father, who sent Me, also testifies about Me.”
texts.asv: I am he that beareth witness of myself, and the Father that sent me beareth witness of me.

texts.webp: They said therefore to him, “Where is your Father?”
texts.bsb: “Where is Your Father?” they asked Him.
texts.asv: They said therefore unto him, Where is thy Father? Jesus answered, Ye know neither me, nor my Father: if ye knew me, ye would know my Father also.

texts.webp: Jesus spoke these words in the treasury, as he taught in the temple. Yet no one arrested him, because his hour had not yet come.
texts.bsb: He spoke these words while teaching in the temple courts, near the treasury. Yet no one seized Him, because His hour had not yet come.
texts.asv: These words spake he in the treasury, as he taught in the temple: and no man took him; because his hour was not yet come.

texts.webp: Jesus said therefore again to them, “I am going away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sins. Where I go, you can’t come.”
texts.bsb: Again He said to them, “I am going away, and you will look for Me, but you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come.”
texts.asv: He said therefore again unto them, I go away, and ye shall seek me, and shall die in your sin: whither I go, ye cannot come.

texts.webp: The Jews therefore said, “Will he kill himself, because he says, ‘Where I am going, you can’t come’?”
texts.bsb: So the Jews began to ask, “Will He kill Himself, since He says, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come’?”
texts.asv: The Jews therefore said, Will he kill himself, that he saith, Whither I go, ye cannot come?

texts.webp: He said to them, “You are from beneath. I am from above. You are of this world. I am not of this world.
texts.bsb: Then He told them, “You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world.
texts.asv: And he said unto them, Ye are from beneath; I am from above: ye are of this world; I am not of this world.

texts.webp: I said therefore to you that you will die in your sins; for unless you believe that I am he, you will die in your sins.”
texts.bsb: That is why I told you that you would die in your sins. For unless you believe that I am He, you will die in your sins.”
texts.asv: I said therefore unto you, that ye shall die in your sins: for except ye believe that I am he, ye shall die in your sins.

texts.webp: They said therefore to him, “Who are you?”
texts.bsb: “Who are You?” they asked.
texts.asv: They said therefore unto him, Who art thou? Jesus said unto them, Even that which I have also spoken unto you from the beginning.

texts.webp: I have many things to speak and to judge concerning you. However, he who sent me is true; and the things which I heard from him, these I say to the world.”
texts.bsb: “I have much to say about you and much to judge. But the One who sent Me is truthful, and what I have heard from Him, I tell the world.”
texts.asv: I have many things to speak and to judge concerning you: howbeit he that sent me is true; and the things which I heard from him, these speak I unto the world.

texts.webp: They didn’t understand that he spoke to them about the Father.
texts.bsb: They did not understand that He was telling them about the Father.
texts.asv: They perceived not that he spake to them of the Father.

texts.webp: Jesus therefore said to them, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he, and I do nothing of myself, but as my Father taught me, I say these things.
texts.bsb: So Jesus said, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am He, and that I do nothing on My own, but speak exactly what the Father has taught Me.
texts.asv: Jesus therefore said, When ye have lifted up the Son of man, then shall ye know that I am he, and that I do nothing of myself, but as the Father taught me, I speak these things.

texts.webp: He who sent me is with me. The Father hasn’t left me alone, for I always do the things that are pleasing to him.”
texts.bsb: He who sent Me is with Me. He has not left Me alone, because I always do what pleases Him.”
texts.asv: And he that sent me is with me; he hath not left me alone; for I do always the things that are pleasing to him.

texts.webp: As he spoke these things, many believed in him.
texts.bsb: As Jesus spoke these things, many believed in Him.
texts.asv: As he spake these things, many believed on him.

texts.webp: Jesus therefore said to those Jews who had believed him, “If you remain in my word, then you are truly my disciples.
texts.bsb: So He said to the Jews who had believed Him, “If you continue in My word, you are truly My disciples.
texts.asv: Jesus therefore said to those Jews that had believed him, If ye abide in my word, then are ye truly my disciples;

texts.webp: You will know the truth, and the truth will make you free.”
texts.bsb: Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.”
texts.asv: and ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

texts.webp: They answered him, “We are Abraham’s offspring, and have never been in bondage to anyone. How do you say, ‘You will be made free’?”
texts.bsb: “We are Abraham’s descendants,” they answered. “We have never been slaves to anyone. How can You say we will be set free?”
texts.asv: They answered unto him, We are Abraham’s seed, and have never yet been in bondage to any man: how sayest thou, Ye shall be made free?

texts.webp: Jesus answered them, “Most certainly I tell you, everyone who commits sin is the bondservant of sin.
texts.bsb: Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, everyone who sins is a slave to sin.
texts.asv: Jesus answered them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Every one that committeth sin is the bondservant of sin.

texts.webp: A bondservant doesn’t live in the house forever. A son remains forever.
texts.bsb: A slave does not remain in the house forever, but a son remains forever.
texts.asv: And the bondservant abideth not in the house for ever: the son abideth for ever.

texts.webp: If therefore the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.
texts.bsb: So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.
texts.asv: If therefore the Son shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.

texts.webp: I know that you are Abraham’s offspring, yet you seek to kill me, because my word finds no place in you.
texts.bsb: I know you are Abraham’s descendants, but you are trying to kill Me because My word has no place within you.
texts.asv: I know that ye are Abraham’s seed; yet ye seek to kill me, because my word hath not free course in you.

texts.webp: I say the things which I have seen with my Father; and you also do the things which you have seen with your father.”
texts.bsb: I speak of what I have seen in the presence of the Father, and you do what you have heard from your father.”
texts.asv: I speak the things which I have seen with my Father: and ye also do the things which ye heard from your father.

texts.webp: They answered him, “Our father is Abraham.”
texts.bsb: “Abraham is our father,” they replied.
texts.asv: They answered and said unto him, Our father is Abraham. Jesus saith unto them, If ye were Abraham’s children, ye would do the works of Abraham.

texts.webp: But now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth which I heard from God. Abraham didn’t do this.
texts.bsb: But now you are trying to kill Me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham never did such a thing.
texts.asv: But now ye seek to kill me, a man that hath told you the truth, which I heard from God: this did not Abraham.

texts.webp: You do the works of your father.”
texts.bsb: You are doing the works of your father.”
texts.asv: Ye do the works of your father. They said unto him, We were not born of fornication; we have one Father, even God.

texts.webp: Therefore Jesus said to them, “If God were your father, you would love me, for I came out and have come from God. For I haven’t come of myself, but he sent me.
texts.bsb: Jesus said to them, “If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I have come here from God. I have not come on My own, but He sent Me.
texts.asv: Jesus said unto them, If God were your Father, ye would love me: for I came forth and am come from God; for neither have I come of myself, but he sent me.

texts.webp: Why don’t you understand my speech? Because you can’t hear my word.
texts.bsb: Why do you not understand what I am saying? It is because you are unable to accept My message.
texts.asv: Why do ye not understand my speech? Even because ye cannot hear my word.

texts.webp: You are of your father the devil, and you want to do the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning, and doesn’t stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks on his own; for he is a liar, and the father of lies.
texts.bsb: You belong to your father, the devil, and you want to carry out his desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, refusing to uphold the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks his native language, because he is a liar and the father of lies.
texts.asv: Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father it is your will to do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and standeth not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father thereof.

texts.webp: But because I tell the truth, you don’t believe me.
texts.bsb: But because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me!
texts.asv: But because I say the truth, ye believe me not.

texts.webp: Which of you convicts me of sin? If I tell the truth, why do you not believe me?
texts.bsb: Which of you can prove Me guilty of sin? If I speak the truth, why do you not believe Me?
texts.asv: Which of you convicteth me of sin? If I say truth, why do ye not believe me?

texts.webp: He who is of God hears the words of God. For this cause you don’t hear, because you are not of God.”
texts.bsb: Whoever belongs to God hears the words of God. The reason you do not hear is that you do not belong to God.”
texts.asv: He that is of God heareth the words of God: for this cause ye hear them not, because ye are not of God.

texts.webp: Then the Jews answered him, “Don’t we say well that you are a Samaritan, and have a demon?”
texts.bsb: The Jews answered Him, “Are we not right to say that You are a Samaritan and You have a demon?”
texts.asv: The Jews answered and said unto him, Say we not well that thou art a Samaritan, and hast a demon?

texts.webp: Jesus answered, “I don’t have a demon, but I honor my Father and you dishonor me.
texts.bsb: “I do not have a demon,” Jesus replied, “but I honor My Father, and you dishonor Me.
texts.asv: Jesus answered, I have not a demon; but I honor my Father, and ye dishonor me.

texts.webp: But I don’t seek my own glory. There is one who seeks and judges.
texts.bsb: I do not seek My own glory. There is One who seeks it, and He is the Judge.
texts.asv: But I seek not mine own glory: there is one that seeketh and judgeth.

texts.webp: Most certainly, I tell you, if a person keeps my word, he will never see death.”
texts.bsb: Truly, truly, I tell you, if anyone keeps My word, he will never see death.”
texts.asv: Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my word, he shall never see death.

texts.webp: Then the Jews said to him, “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham died, as did the prophets; and you say, ‘If a man keeps my word, he will never taste of death.’
texts.bsb: “Now we know that You have a demon!” declared the Jews. “Abraham died, and so did the prophets, yet You say that anyone who keeps Your word will never taste death.
texts.asv: The Jews said unto him, Now we know that thou hast a demon. Abraham died, and the prophets; and thou sayest, If a man keep my word, he shall never taste of death.

texts.webp: Are you greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets died. Who do you make yourself out to be?”
texts.bsb: Are You greater than our father Abraham? He died, as did the prophets. Who do You claim to be?”
texts.asv: Art thou greater than our father Abraham, who died? and the prophets died: whom makest thou thyself?

texts.webp: Jesus answered, “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, of whom you say that he is our God.
texts.bsb: Jesus answered, “If I glorify Myself, My glory means nothing. The One who glorifies Me is My Father, of whom you say, ‘He is our God.’
texts.asv: Jesus answered, If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing: it is my Father that glorifieth me; of whom ye say, that he is your God;

texts.webp: You have not known him, but I know him. If I said, ‘I don’t know him,’ I would be like you, a liar. But I know him and keep his word.
texts.bsb: You do not know Him, but I know Him. If I said I did not know Him, I would be a liar like you. But I do know Him, and I keep His word.
texts.asv: and ye have not known him: but I know him; and if I should say, I know him not, I shall be like unto you, a liar: but I know him, and keep his word.

texts.webp: Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day. He saw it and was glad.”
texts.bsb: Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see My day. He saw it and was glad.”
texts.asv: Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day; and he saw it, and was glad.

texts.webp: The Jews therefore said to him, “You are not yet fifty years old! Have you seen Abraham?”
texts.bsb: Then the Jews said to Him, “You are not yet fifty years old, and You have seen Abraham?”
texts.asv: The Jews therefore said unto him, Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham?

texts.webp: Jesus said to them, “Most certainly, I tell you, before Abraham came into existence, I AM. ”
texts.bsb: “Truly, truly, I tell you,” Jesus declared, “before Abraham was born, I am! ”
texts.asv: Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was born, I am.

texts.webp: Therefore they took up stones to throw at him, but Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple, having gone through the middle of them, and so passed by.
texts.bsb: At this, they picked up stones to throw at Him. But Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple area.
texts.asv: They took up stones therefore to cast at him: but Jesus hid himself, and went out of the temple.

texts.webp: As he passed by, he saw a man blind from birth.
texts.bsb: Now as Jesus was passing by, He saw a man blind from birth,
texts.asv: And as he passed by, he saw a man blind from his birth.

texts.webp: His disciples asked him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?”
texts.bsb: and His disciples asked Him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?”
texts.asv: And his disciples asked him, saying, Rabbi, who sinned, this man, or his parents, that he should be born blind?

texts.webp: Jesus answered, “This man didn’t sin, nor did his parents, but that the works of God might be revealed in him.
texts.bsb: Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but this happened so that the works of God would be displayed in him.
texts.asv: Jesus answered, Neither did this man sin, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him.

texts.webp: I must work the works of him who sent me while it is day. The night is coming, when no one can work.
texts.bsb: While it is daytime, we must do the works of Him who sent Me. Night is coming, when no one can work.
texts.asv: We must work the works of him that sent me, while it is day: the night cometh, when no man can work.

texts.webp: While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”
texts.bsb: While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”
texts.asv: When I am in the world, I am the light of the world.

texts.webp: When he had said this, he spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, anointed the blind man’s eyes with the mud,
texts.bsb: When Jesus had said this, He spit on the ground, made some mud, and applied it to the man’s eyes.
texts.asv: When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and anointed his eyes with the clay,

texts.webp: and said to him, “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam” (which means “Sent”). So he went away, washed, and came back seeing.
texts.bsb: Then He told him, “Go, wash in the Pool of Siloam” (which means “Sent”). So the man went and washed, and came back seeing.
texts.asv: and said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam (which is by interpretation, Sent). He went away therefore, and washed, and came seeing.

texts.webp: Therefore the neighbors and those who saw that he was blind before said, “Isn’t this he who sat and begged?”
texts.bsb: At this, his neighbors and those who had formerly seen him begging began to ask, “Isn’t this the man who used to sit and beg?”
texts.asv: The neighbors therefore, and they that saw him aforetime, that he was a beggar, said, Is not this he that sat and begged?

texts.webp: Others were saying, “It is he.” Still others were saying, “He looks like him.”
texts.bsb: Some claimed that he was, but others said, “No, he just looks like him.”
texts.asv: Others said, It is he: others said, No, but he is like him. He said, I am he.

texts.webp: They therefore were asking him, “How were your eyes opened?”
texts.bsb: “How then were your eyes opened?” they asked.
texts.asv: They said therefore unto him, How then were thine eyes opened?

texts.webp: He answered, “A man called Jesus made mud, anointed my eyes, and said to me, ‘Go to the pool of Siloam and wash.’ So I went away and washed, and I received sight.”
texts.bsb: He answered, “The man they call Jesus made some mud and anointed my eyes, and He told me to go to Siloam and wash. So I went and washed and received my sight.”
texts.asv: He answered, The man that is called Jesus made clay, and anointed mine eyes, and said unto me, Go to Siloam, and wash: so I went away and washed, and I received sight.

texts.webp: Then they asked him, “Where is he?”
texts.bsb: “Where is He?” they asked.
texts.asv: And they said unto him, Where is he? He saith, I know not.

texts.webp: They brought him who had been blind to the Pharisees.
texts.bsb: They brought to the Pharisees the man who had been blind.
texts.asv: They bring to the Pharisees him that aforetime was blind.

texts.webp: It was a Sabbath when Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes.
texts.bsb: Now the day on which Jesus had made the mud and opened his eyes was a Sabbath.
texts.asv: Now it was the sabbath on the day when Jesus made the clay, and opened his eyes.

texts.webp: Again therefore the Pharisees also asked him how he received his sight. He said to them, “He put mud on my eyes, I washed, and I see.”
texts.bsb: So the Pharisees also asked him how he had received his sight.
texts.asv: Again therefore the Pharisees also asked him how he received his sight. And he said unto them, He put clay upon mine eyes, and I washed, and I see.

texts.webp: Some therefore of the Pharisees said, “This man is not from God, because he doesn’t keep the Sabbath.”
texts.bsb: Because of this, some of the Pharisees said, “This man is not from God, for He does not keep the Sabbath.”
texts.asv: Some therefore of the Pharisees said, This man is not from God, because he keepeth not the sabbath. But others said, How can a man that is a sinner do such signs? And there was a division among them.

texts.webp: Therefore they asked the blind man again, “What do you say about him, because he opened your eyes?”
texts.bsb: So once again they asked the man who had been blind, “What do you say about Him, since it was your eyes He opened?”
texts.asv: They say therefore unto the blind man again, What sayest thou of him, in that he opened thine eyes? And he said, He is a prophet.

texts.webp: The Jews therefore didn’t believe concerning him, that he had been blind and had received his sight, until they called the parents of him who had received his sight,
texts.bsb: The Jews still did not believe that the man had been blind and had received his sight until they summoned his parents
texts.asv: The Jews therefore did not believe concerning him, that he had been blind, and had received his sight, until they called the parents of him that had received his sight,

texts.webp: and asked them, “Is this your son, whom you say was born blind? How then does he now see?”
texts.bsb: and asked, “Is this your son, the one you say was born blind? So how is it that he can now see?”
texts.asv: and asked them, saying, Is this your son, who ye say was born blind? how then doth he now see?

texts.webp: His parents answered them, “We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind;
texts.bsb: His parents answered, “We know he is our son, and we know he was born blind.
texts.asv: His parents answered and said, We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind:

texts.webp: but how he now sees, we don’t know; or who opened his eyes, we don’t know. He is of age. Ask him. He will speak for himself.”
texts.bsb: But how he can now see or who opened his eyes, we do not know. Ask him. He is old enough to speak for himself.”
texts.asv: but how he now seeth, we know not; or who opened his eyes, we know not: ask him; he is of age; he shall speak for himself.

texts.webp: His parents said these things because they feared the Jews; for the Jews had already agreed that if any man would confess him as Christ, he would be put out of the synagogue.
texts.bsb: His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews. For the Jews had already determined that anyone who confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue.
texts.asv: These things said his parents, because they feared the Jews: for the Jews had agreed already, that if any man should confess him to be Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue.

texts.webp: Therefore his parents said, “He is of age. Ask him.”
texts.bsb: That was why his parents said, “He is old enough. Ask him.”
texts.asv: Therefore said his parents, He is of age; ask him.

texts.webp: So they called the man who was blind a second time, and said to him, “Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.”
texts.bsb: So a second time they called for the man who had been blind and said, “Give glory to God! We know that this man is a sinner.”
texts.asv: So they called a second time the man that was blind, and said unto him, Give glory to God: we know that this man is a sinner.

texts.webp: He therefore answered, “I don’t know if he is a sinner. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”
texts.bsb: He answered, “Whether He is a sinner I do not know. There is one thing I do know: I was blind, but now I see!”
texts.asv: He therefore answered, Whether he is a sinner, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.

texts.webp: They said to him again, “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?”
texts.bsb: “What did He do to you?” they asked. “How did He open your eyes?”
texts.asv: They said therefore unto him, What did he to thee? how opened he thine eyes?

texts.webp: He answered them, “I told you already, and you didn’t listen. Why do you want to hear it again? You don’t also want to become his disciples, do you?”
texts.bsb: He replied, “I already told you, and you did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you also want to become His disciples?”
texts.asv: He answered them, I told you even now, and ye did not hear; wherefore would ye hear it again? would ye also become his disciples?

texts.webp: They insulted him and said, “You are his disciple, but we are disciples of Moses.
texts.bsb: Then they heaped insults on him and said, “You are His disciple; we are disciples of Moses.
texts.asv: And they reviled him, and said, Thou art his disciple; but we are disciples of Moses.

texts.webp: We know that God has spoken to Moses. But as for this man, we don’t know where he comes from.”
texts.bsb: We know that God spoke to Moses, but we do not know where this man is from.”
texts.asv: We know that God hath spoken unto Moses: but as for this man, we know not whence he is.

texts.webp: The man answered them, “How amazing! You don’t know where he comes from, yet he opened my eyes.
texts.bsb: “That is remarkable indeed!” the man said. “You do not know where He is from, and yet He opened my eyes.
texts.asv: The man answered and said unto them, Why, herein is the marvel, that ye know not whence he is, and yet he opened mine eyes.

texts.webp: We know that God doesn’t listen to sinners, but if anyone is a worshiper of God and does his will, he listens to him.
texts.bsb: We know that God does not listen to sinners, but He does listen to the one who worships Him and does His will.
texts.asv: We know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and do his will, him he heareth.

texts.webp: Since the world began it has never been heard of that anyone opened the eyes of someone born blind.
texts.bsb: Never before has anyone heard of opening the eyes of a man born blind.
texts.asv: Since the world began it was never heard that any one opened the eyes of a man born blind.

texts.webp: If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.”
texts.bsb: If this man were not from God, He could do no such thing.”
texts.asv: If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.

texts.webp: They answered him, “You were altogether born in sins, and do you teach us?” Then they threw him out.
texts.bsb: They replied, “You were born in utter sin, and you are instructing us?” And they threw him out.
texts.asv: They answered and said unto him, Thou wast altogether born in sins, and dost thou teach us? And they cast him out.

texts.webp: Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, and finding him, he said, “Do you believe in the Son of God?”
texts.bsb: When Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, He found the man and said, “Do you believe in the Son of Man ?”
texts.asv: Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and finding him, he said, Dost thou believe on the Son of God?

texts.webp: He answered, “Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?”
texts.bsb: “Who is He, Sir?” he replied. “Tell me so that I may believe in Him.”
texts.asv: He answered and said, And who is he, Lord, that I may believe on him?

texts.webp: Jesus said to him, “You have both seen him, and it is he who speaks with you.”
texts.bsb: “You have already seen Him,” Jesus answered. “He is the One speaking with you.”
texts.asv: Jesus said unto him, Thou hast both seen him, and he it is that speaketh with thee.

texts.webp: He said, “Lord, I believe!” and he worshiped him.
texts.bsb: “Lord, I believe,” he said. And he worshiped Jesus.
texts.asv: And he said, Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him.

texts.webp: Jesus said, “I came into this world for judgment, that those who don’t see may see; and that those who see may become blind.”
texts.bsb: Then Jesus declared, “For judgment I have come into this world, so that the blind may see and those who see may become blind.”
texts.asv: And Jesus said, For judgment came I into this world, that they that see not may see; and that they that see may become blind.

texts.webp: Those of the Pharisees who were with him heard these things, and said to him, “Are we also blind?”
texts.bsb: Some of the Pharisees who were with Him heard this, and they asked Him, “Are we blind too?”
texts.asv: Those of the Pharisees who were with him heard these things, and said unto him, Are we also blind?

texts.webp: Jesus said to them, “If you were blind, you would have no sin; but now you say, ‘We see.’ Therefore your sin remains.
texts.bsb: “If you were blind,” Jesus replied, “you would not be guilty of sin. But since you claim you can see, your guilt remains.”
texts.asv: Jesus said unto them, If ye were blind, ye would have no sin: but now ye say, We see: your sin remaineth.

texts.webp: “Most certainly, I tell you, one who doesn’t enter by the door into the sheep fold, but climbs up some other way, is a thief and a robber.
texts.bsb: “Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever does not enter the sheepfold by the gate, but climbs in some other way, is a thief and a robber.
texts.asv: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door into the fold of the sheep, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber.

texts.webp: But one who enters in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
texts.bsb: But the one who enters by the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.
texts.asv: But he that entereth in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.

texts.webp: The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
texts.bsb: The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen for his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
texts.asv: To him the porter openeth; and the sheep hear his voice: and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out.

texts.webp: Whenever he brings out his own sheep, he goes before them; and the sheep follow him, for they know his voice.
texts.bsb: When he has brought out all his own, he goes on ahead of them, and his sheep follow him because they know his voice.
texts.asv: When he hath put forth all his own, he goeth before them, and the sheep follow him: for they know his voice.

texts.webp: They will by no means follow a stranger, but will flee from him; for they don’t know the voice of strangers.”
texts.bsb: But they will never follow a stranger; in fact, they will flee from him because they do not recognize his voice.”
texts.asv: And a stranger will they not follow, but will flee from him: for they know not the voice of strangers.

texts.webp: Jesus spoke this parable to them, but they didn’t understand what he was telling them.
texts.bsb: Jesus spoke to them using this illustration, but they did not understand what He was telling them.
texts.asv: This parable spake Jesus unto them: but they understood not what things they were which he spake unto them.

texts.webp: Jesus therefore said to them again, “Most certainly, I tell you, I am the sheep’s door.
texts.bsb: So He said to them again, “Truly, truly, I tell you, I am the gate for the sheep.
texts.asv: Jesus therefore said unto them again, Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep.

texts.webp: All who came before me are thieves and robbers, but the sheep didn’t listen to them.
texts.bsb: All who came before Me were thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.
texts.asv: All that came before me are thieves and robbers: but the sheep did not hear them.

texts.webp: I am the door. If anyone enters in by me, he will be saved, and will go in and go out and will find pasture.
texts.bsb: I am the gate. If anyone enters through Me, he will be saved. He will come in and go out and find pasture.
texts.asv: I am the door; by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and go out, and shall find pasture.

texts.webp: The thief only comes to steal, kill, and destroy. I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.
texts.bsb: The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I have come that they may have life, and have it in all its fullness.
texts.asv: The thief cometh not, but that he may steal, and kill, and destroy: I came that they may have life, and may have it abundantly.

texts.webp: “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
texts.bsb: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down His life for the sheep.
texts.asv: I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd layeth down his life for the sheep.

texts.webp: He who is a hired hand, and not a shepherd, who doesn’t own the sheep, sees the wolf coming, leaves the sheep, and flees. The wolf snatches the sheep and scatters them.
texts.bsb: The hired hand is not the shepherd, and the sheep are not his own. When he sees the wolf coming, he abandons the sheep and runs away. Then the wolf pounces on them and scatters the flock.
texts.asv: He that is a hireling, and not a shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, beholdeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth, and the wolf snatcheth them, and scattereth them:

texts.webp: The hired hand flees because he is a hired hand and doesn’t care for the sheep.
texts.bsb: The man runs away because he is a hired servant and is unconcerned for the sheep.
texts.asv: he fleeth because he is a hireling, and careth not for the sheep.

texts.webp: I am the good shepherd. I know my own, and I’m known by my own;
texts.bsb: I am the good shepherd. I know My sheep and My sheep know Me,
texts.asv: I am the good shepherd; and I know mine own, and mine own know me,

texts.webp: even as the Father knows me, and I know the Father. I lay down my life for the sheep.
texts.bsb: just as the Father knows Me and I know the Father. And I lay down My life for the sheep.
texts.asv: even as the Father knoweth me, and I know the Father; and I lay down my life for the sheep.

texts.webp: I have other sheep which are not of this fold. I must bring them also, and they will hear my voice. They will become one flock with one shepherd.
texts.bsb: I have other sheep that are not of this fold. I must bring them in as well, and they will listen to My voice. Then there will be one flock and one shepherd.
texts.asv: And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and they shall become one flock, one shepherd.

texts.webp: Therefore the Father loves me, because I lay down my life, that I may take it again.
texts.bsb: The reason the Father loves Me is that I lay down My life in order to take it up again.
texts.asv: Therefore doth the Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I may take it again.

texts.webp: No one takes it away from me, but I lay it down by myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. I received this commandment from my Father.”
texts.bsb: No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of My own accord. I have authority to lay it down and authority to take it up again. This charge I have received from My Father.”
texts.asv: No one taketh it away from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commandment received I from my Father.

texts.webp: Therefore a division arose again among the Jews because of these words.
texts.bsb: Again there was division among the Jews because of Jesus’ message.
texts.asv: There arose a division again among the Jews because of these words.

texts.webp: Many of them said, “He has a demon and is insane! Why do you listen to him?”
texts.bsb: Many of them said, “He is demon-possessed and insane. Why would you listen to Him?”
texts.asv: And many of them said, He hath a demon, and is mad; why hear ye him?

texts.webp: Others said, “These are not the sayings of one possessed by a demon. It isn’t possible for a demon to open the eyes of the blind, is it?”
texts.bsb: But others replied, “These are not the words of a man possessed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?”
texts.asv: Others said, These are not the sayings of one possessed with a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?

texts.webp: It was the Feast of the Dedication at Jerusalem.
texts.bsb: At that time the Feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem. It was winter,
texts.asv: And it was the feast of the dedication at Jerusalem:

texts.webp: It was winter, and Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon’s porch.
texts.bsb: and Jesus was walking in the temple courts in Solomon’s Colonnade.
texts.asv: it was winter; and Jesus was walking in the temple in Solomon’s porch.

texts.webp: The Jews therefore came around him and said to him, “How long will you hold us in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.”
texts.bsb: So the Jews gathered around Him and demanded, “How long will You keep us in suspense? If You are the Christ, tell us plainly.”
texts.asv: The Jews therefore came round about him, and said unto him, How long dost thou hold us in suspense? If thou art the Christ, tell us plainly.

texts.webp: Jesus answered them, “I told you, and you don’t believe. The works that I do in my Father’s name, these testify about me.
texts.bsb: “I already told you,” Jesus replied, “but you did not believe. The works I do in My Father’s name testify on My behalf.
texts.asv: Jesus answered them, I told you, and ye believe not: the works that I do in my Father’s name, these bear witness of me.

texts.webp: But you don’t believe, because you are not of my sheep, as I told you.
texts.bsb: But because you are not My sheep, you refuse to believe.
texts.asv: But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep.

texts.webp: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.
texts.bsb: My sheep listen to My voice; I know them, and they follow Me.
texts.asv: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:

texts.webp: I give eternal life to them. They will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand.
texts.bsb: I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one can snatch them out of My hand.
texts.asv: and I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, and no one shall snatch them out of my hand.

texts.webp: My Father who has given them to me is greater than all. No one is able to snatch them out of my Father’s hand.
texts.bsb: My Father who has given them to Me is greater than all. No one can snatch them out of My Father’s hand.
texts.asv: My Father, who hath given them unto me, is greater than all; and no one is able to snatch them out of the Father’s hand.

texts.webp: I and the Father are one.”
texts.bsb: I and the Father are one.”
texts.asv: I and the Father are one.

texts.webp: Therefore the Jews took up stones again to stone him.
texts.bsb: At this, the Jews again picked up stones to stone Him.
texts.asv: The Jews took up stones again to stone him.

texts.webp: Jesus answered them, “I have shown you many good works from my Father. For which of those works do you stone me?”
texts.bsb: But Jesus responded, “I have shown you many good works from the Father. For which of these do you stone Me?”
texts.asv: Jesus answered them, Many good works have I showed you from the Father; for which of those works do ye stone me?

texts.webp: The Jews answered him, “We don’t stone you for a good work, but for blasphemy, because you, being a man, make yourself God.”
texts.bsb: “We are not stoning You for any good work,” said the Jews, “but for blasphemy, because You, who are a man, make Yourself out to be God.”
texts.asv: The Jews answered him, For a good work we stone thee not, but for blasphemy; and because that thou, being a man, makest thyself God.

texts.webp: Jesus answered them, “Isn’t it written in your law, ‘I said, you are gods’?
texts.bsb: Jesus replied, “Is it not written in your Law: ‘I have said you are gods’ ?
