texts.asv: Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods?

texts.webp: If he called them gods, to whom the word of God came (and the Scripture can’t be broken),
texts.bsb: If he called them gods to whom the word of God came — and the Scripture cannot be broken —
texts.asv: If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came (and the scripture cannot be broken),

texts.webp: do you say of him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, ‘You blaspheme,’ because I said, ‘I am the Son of God’?
texts.bsb: then what about the One whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world? How then can you accuse Me of blasphemy for stating that I am the Son of God?
texts.asv: say ye of him, whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, Thou blasphemest; because I said, I am the Son of God?

texts.webp: If I don’t do the works of my Father, don’t believe me.
texts.bsb: If I am not doing the works of My Father, then do not believe Me.
texts.asv: If I do not the works of my Father, believe me not.

texts.webp: But if I do them, though you don’t believe me, believe the works, that you may know and believe that the Father is in me, and I in the Father.”
texts.bsb: But if I am doing them, even though you do not believe Me, believe the works themselves, so that you may know and understand that the Father is in Me, and I am in the Father.”
texts.asv: But if I do them, though ye believe not me, believe the works: that ye may know and understand that the Father is in me, and I in the Father.

texts.webp: They sought again to seize him, and he went out of their hand.
texts.bsb: At this, they tried again to seize Him, but He escaped their grasp.
texts.asv: They sought again to take him: and he went forth out of their hand.

texts.webp: He went away again beyond the Jordan into the place where John was baptizing at first, and he stayed there.
texts.bsb: Then Jesus went back across the Jordan to the place where John had first been baptizing, and He stayed there.
texts.asv: And he went away again beyond the Jordan into the place where John was at the first baptizing; and there he abode.

texts.webp: Many came to him. They said, “John indeed did no sign, but everything that John said about this man is true.”
texts.bsb: Many came to Him and said, “Although John never performed a sign, everything he said about this man was true.”
texts.asv: And many came unto him; and they said, John indeed did no sign: but all things whatsoever John spake of this man were true.

texts.webp: Many believed in him there.
texts.bsb: And many in that place believed in Jesus.
texts.asv: And many believed on him there.

texts.webp: Now a certain man was sick, Lazarus from Bethany, of the village of Mary and her sister, Martha.
texts.bsb: At this time a man named Lazarus was sick. He lived in Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha.
texts.asv: Now a certain man was sick, Lazarus of Bethany, of the village of Mary and her sister Martha.

texts.webp: It was that Mary who had anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick.
texts.bsb: (Mary, whose brother Lazarus was sick, was to anoint the Lord with perfume and wipe His feet with her hair.)
texts.asv: And it was that Mary who anointed the Lord with ointment, and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick.

texts.webp: The sisters therefore sent to him, saying, “Lord, behold, he for whom you have great affection is sick.”
texts.bsb: So the sisters sent word to Jesus, “Lord, the one You love is sick.”
texts.asv: The sisters therefore sent unto him, saying, Lord, behold, he whom thou lovest is sick.

texts.webp: But when Jesus heard it, he said, “This sickness is not to death, but for the glory of God, that God’s Son may be glorified by it.”
texts.bsb: When Jesus heard this, He said, “This sickness will not end in death. No, it is for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it.”
texts.asv: But when Jesus heard it, he said, This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God may be glorified thereby.

texts.webp: Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus.
texts.bsb: Now Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.
texts.asv: Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus.

texts.webp: When therefore he heard that he was sick, he stayed two days in the place where he was.
texts.bsb: So on hearing that Lazarus was sick, He stayed where He was for two days,
texts.asv: When therefore he heard that he was sick, he abode at that time two days in the place where he was.

texts.webp: Then after this he said to the disciples, “Let’s go into Judea again.”
texts.bsb: and then He said to the disciples, “Let us go back to Judea.”
texts.asv: Then after this he saith to the disciples, Let us go into Judæa again.

texts.webp: The disciples asked him, “Rabbi, the Jews were just trying to stone you. Are you going there again?”
texts.bsb: “Rabbi,” they replied, “the Jews just tried to stone You, and You are going back there?”
texts.asv: The disciples say unto him, Rabbi, the Jews were but now seeking to stone thee; and goest thou thither again?

texts.webp: Jesus answered, “Aren’t there twelve hours of daylight? If a man walks in the day, he doesn’t stumble, because he sees the light of this world.
texts.bsb: Jesus answered, “Are there not twelve hours of daylight? If anyone walks in the daytime, he will not stumble, because he sees by the light of this world.
texts.asv: Jesus answered, Are there not twelve hours in the day? If a man walk in the day, he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of this world.

texts.webp: But if a man walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light isn’t in him.”
texts.bsb: But if anyone walks at night, he will stumble, because he has no light.”
texts.asv: But if a man walk in the night, he stumbleth, because the light is not in him.

texts.webp: He said these things, and after that, he said to them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going so that I may awake him out of sleep.”
texts.bsb: After He had said this, He told them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up.”
texts.asv: These things spake he: and after this he saith unto them, Our friend Lazarus is fallen asleep; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.

texts.webp: The disciples therefore said, “Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will recover.”
texts.bsb: His disciples replied, “Lord, if he is sleeping, he will get better.”
texts.asv: The disciples therefore said unto him, Lord, if he is fallen asleep, he will recover.

texts.webp: Now Jesus had spoken of his death, but they thought that he spoke of taking rest in sleep.
texts.bsb: They thought that Jesus was talking about actual sleep, but He was speaking about the death of Lazarus.
texts.asv: Now Jesus had spoken of his death: but they thought that he spake of taking rest in sleep.

texts.webp: So Jesus said to them plainly then, “Lazarus is dead.
texts.bsb: So Jesus told them plainly, “Lazarus is dead,
texts.asv: Then Jesus therefore said unto them plainly, Lazarus is dead.

texts.webp: I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, so that you may believe. Nevertheless, let’s go to him.”
texts.bsb: and for your sake I am glad I was not there, so that you may believe. But let us go to him.”
texts.asv: And I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, to the intent ye may believe; nevertheless let us go unto him.

texts.webp: Thomas therefore, who is called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples, “Let’s also go, that we may die with him.”
texts.bsb: Then Thomas called Didymus said to his fellow disciples, “Let us also go, so that we may die with Him.”
texts.asv: Thomas therefore, who is called Didymus, said unto his fellow-disciples, Let us also go, that we may die with him.

texts.webp: So when Jesus came, he found that he had been in the tomb four days already.
texts.bsb: When Jesus arrived, He found that Lazarus had already spent four days in the tomb.
texts.asv: So when Jesus came, he found that he had been in the tomb four days already.

texts.webp: Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.
texts.bsb: Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, a little less than two miles away,
texts.asv: Now Bethany was nigh unto Jerusalem, about fifteen furlongs off;

texts.webp: Many of the Jews had joined the women around Martha and Mary, to console them concerning their brother.
texts.bsb: and many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them in the loss of their brother.
texts.asv: and many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary, to console them concerning their brother.

texts.webp: Then when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went and met him, but Mary stayed in the house.
texts.bsb: So when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet Him, but Mary stayed at home.
texts.asv: Martha therefore, when she heard that Jesus was coming, went and met him: but Mary still sat in the house.

texts.webp: Therefore Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.
texts.bsb: Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.
texts.asv: Martha therefore said unto Jesus, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.

texts.webp: Even now I know that whatever you ask of God, God will give you.”
texts.bsb: But even now I know that God will give You whatever You ask of Him.”
texts.asv: And even now I know that, whatsoever thou shalt ask of God, God will give thee.

texts.webp: Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise again.”
texts.bsb: “Your brother will rise again,” Jesus told her.
texts.asv: Jesus saith unto her, Thy brother shall rise again.

texts.webp: Martha said to him, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”
texts.bsb: Martha replied, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”
texts.asv: Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.

texts.webp: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies.
texts.bsb: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in Me will live, even though he dies.
texts.asv: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth on me, though he die, yet shall he live;

texts.webp: Whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”
texts.bsb: And everyone who lives and believes in Me will never die. Do you believe this?”
texts.asv: and whosoever liveth and believeth on me shall never die. Believest thou this?

texts.webp: She said to him, “Yes, Lord. I have come to believe that you are the Christ, God’s Son, he who comes into the world.”
texts.bsb: “Yes, Lord,” she answered, “I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God, who was to come into the world.”
texts.asv: She saith unto him, Yea, Lord: I have believed that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, even he that cometh into the world.

texts.webp: When she had said this, she went away and called Mary, her sister, secretly, saying, “The Teacher is here and is calling you.”
texts.bsb: After Martha had said this, she went back and called her sister Mary aside to tell her, “The Teacher is here and is asking for you.”
texts.asv: And when she had said this, she went away, and called Mary her sister secretly, saying, The Teacher is here, and calleth thee.

texts.webp: When she heard this, she arose quickly and went to him.
texts.bsb: And when Mary heard this, she got up quickly and went to Him.
texts.asv: And she, when she heard it, arose quickly, and went unto him.

texts.webp: Now Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was in the place where Martha met him.
texts.bsb: Now Jesus had not yet entered the village, but was still at the place where Martha had met Him.
texts.asv: (Now Jesus was not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha met him.)

texts.webp: Then the Jews who were with her in the house and were consoling her, when they saw Mary, that she rose up quickly and went out, followed her, saying, “She is going to the tomb to weep there.”
texts.bsb: When the Jews who were in the house consoling Mary saw how quickly she got up and went out, they followed her, supposing she was going to the tomb to mourn there.
texts.asv: The Jews then who were with her in the house, and were consoling her, when they saw Mary, that she rose up quickly and went out, followed her, supposing that she was going unto the tomb to weep there.

texts.webp: Therefore when Mary came to where Jesus was and saw him, she fell down at his feet, saying to him, “Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.”
texts.bsb: When Mary came to Jesus and saw Him, she fell at His feet and said, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.”
texts.asv: Mary therefore, when she came where Jesus was, and saw him, fell down at his feet, saying unto him, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.

texts.webp: When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews weeping who came with her, he groaned in the spirit and was troubled,
texts.bsb: When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also weeping, He was deeply moved in spirit and troubled.
texts.asv: When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews also weeping who came with her, he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled,

texts.webp: and said, “Where have you laid him?”
texts.bsb: “Where have you put him?” He asked.
texts.asv: and said, Where have ye laid him? They say unto him, Lord, come and see.

texts.webp: Jesus wept.
texts.bsb: Jesus wept.
texts.asv: Jesus wept.

texts.webp: The Jews therefore said, “See how much affection he had for him!”
texts.bsb: Then the Jews said, “See how He loved him!”
texts.asv: The Jews therefore said, Behold how he loved him!

texts.webp: Some of them said, “Couldn’t this man, who opened the eyes of him who was blind, have also kept this man from dying?”
texts.bsb: But some of them asked, “Could not this man who opened the eyes of the blind also have kept Lazarus from dying?”
texts.asv: But some of them said, Could not this man, who opened the eyes of him that was blind, have caused that this man also should not die?

texts.webp: Jesus therefore, again groaning in himself, came to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone lay against it.
texts.bsb: Jesus, once again deeply moved, came to the tomb. It was a cave with a stone laid across the entrance.
texts.asv: Jesus therefore again groaning in himself cometh to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone lay against it.

texts.webp: Jesus said, “Take away the stone.”
texts.bsb: “Take away the stone,” Jesus said.
texts.asv: Jesus saith, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto him, Lord, by this time the body decayeth; for he hath been dead four days.

texts.webp: Jesus said to her, “Didn’t I tell you that if you believed, you would see God’s glory?”
texts.bsb: Jesus replied, “Did I not tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?”
texts.asv: Jesus saith unto her, Said I not unto thee, that, if thou believedst, thou shouldest see the glory of God?

texts.webp: So they took away the stone from the place where the dead man was lying. Jesus lifted up his eyes and said, “Father, I thank you that you listened to me.
texts.bsb: So they took away the stone. Then Jesus lifted His eyes upward and said, “Father, I thank You that You have heard Me.
texts.asv: So they took away the stone. And Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou heardest me.

texts.webp: I know that you always listen to me, but because of the multitude standing around I said this, that they may believe that you sent me.”
texts.bsb: I knew that You always hear Me, but I say this for the benefit of the people standing here, so they may believe that You sent Me.”
texts.asv: And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the multitude that standeth around I said it, that they may believe that thou didst send me.

texts.webp: When he had said this, he cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”
texts.bsb: After Jesus had said this, He called out in a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”
texts.asv: And when he had thus spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.

texts.webp: He who was dead came out, bound hand and foot with wrappings, and his face was wrapped around with a cloth.
texts.bsb: The man who had been dead came out with his hands and feet bound in strips of linen, and his face wrapped in a cloth.
texts.asv: He that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with grave-clothes; and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go.

texts.webp: Therefore many of the Jews who came to Mary and saw what Jesus did believed in him.
texts.bsb: Therefore many of the Jews who had come to Mary, and had seen what Jesus did, believed in Him.
texts.asv: Many therefore of the Jews, who came to Mary and beheld that which he did, believed on him.

texts.webp: But some of them went away to the Pharisees and told them the things which Jesus had done.
texts.bsb: But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
texts.asv: But some of them went away to the Pharisees, and told them the things which Jesus had done.

texts.webp: The chief priests therefore and the Pharisees gathered a council, and said, “What are we doing? For this man does many signs.
texts.bsb: Then the chief priests and Pharisees convened the Sanhedrin and said, “What are we to do? This man is performing many signs.
texts.asv: The chief priests therefore and the Pharisees gathered a council, and said, What do we? for this man doeth many signs.

texts.webp: If we leave him alone like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.”
texts.bsb: If we let Him go on like this, everyone will believe in Him, and then the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.”
texts.asv: If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.

texts.webp: But a certain one of them, Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said to them, “You know nothing at all,
texts.bsb: But one of them, named Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them, “You know nothing at all!
texts.asv: But a certain one of them, Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all,

texts.webp: nor do you consider that it is advantageous for us that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation not perish.”
texts.bsb: You do not realize that it is better for you that one man die for the people than that the whole nation perish.”
texts.asv: nor do ye take account that it is expedient for you that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.

texts.webp: Now he didn’t say this of himself, but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation,
texts.bsb: Caiaphas did not say this on his own. Instead, as high priest that year, he was prophesying that Jesus would die for the nation,
texts.asv: Now this he said not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for the nation;

texts.webp: and not for the nation only, but that he might also gather together into one the children of God who are scattered abroad.
texts.bsb: and not only for the nation, but also for the scattered children of God, to gather them together into one.
texts.asv: and not for the nation only, but that he might also gather together into one the children of God that are scattered abroad.

texts.webp: So from that day forward they took counsel that they might put him to death.
texts.bsb: So from that day on they plotted to kill Him.
texts.asv: So from that day forth they took counsel that they might put him to death.

texts.webp: Jesus therefore walked no more openly among the Jews, but departed from there into the country near the wilderness, to a city called Ephraim. He stayed there with his disciples.
texts.bsb: As a result, Jesus no longer went about publicly among the Jews, but He withdrew to a town called Ephraim in an area near the wilderness. And He stayed there with the disciples.
texts.asv: Jesus therefore walked no more openly among the Jews, but departed thence into the country near to the wilderness, into a city called Ephraim; and there he tarried with the disciples.

texts.webp: Now the Passover of the Jews was at hand. Many went up from the country to Jerusalem before the Passover, to purify themselves.
texts.bsb: Now the Jewish Passover was near, and many people went up from the country to Jerusalem to purify themselves before the Passover.
texts.asv: Now the passover of the Jews was at hand: and many went up to Jerusalem out of the country before the passover, to purify themselves.

texts.webp: Then they sought for Jesus and spoke with one another as they stood in the temple, “What do you think—that he isn’t coming to the feast at all?”
texts.bsb: They kept looking for Jesus and asking one another as they stood in the temple courts, “What do you think? Will He come to the feast at all?”
texts.asv: They sought therefore for Jesus, and spake one with another, as they stood in the temple, What think ye? That he will not come to the feast?

texts.webp: Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had commanded that if anyone knew where he was, he should report it, that they might seize him.
texts.bsb: But the chief priests and Pharisees had given orders that anyone who knew where He was must report it, so that they could arrest Him.
texts.asv: Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had given commandment, that, if any man knew where he was, he should show it, that they might take him.

texts.webp: Then, six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, who had been dead, whom he raised from the dead.
texts.bsb: Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, the hometown of Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.
texts.asv: Jesus therefore six days before the passover came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom Jesus raised from the dead.

texts.webp: So they made him a supper there. Martha served, but Lazarus was one of those who sat at the table with him.
texts.bsb: So they hosted a dinner for Jesus there. Martha served, and Lazarus was among those reclining at the table with Him.
texts.asv: So they made him a supper there: and Martha served; but Lazarus was one of them that sat at meat with him.

texts.webp: Therefore Mary took a pound of ointment of pure nard, very precious, and anointed Jesus’ feet and wiped his feet with her hair. The house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.
texts.bsb: Then Mary took about a pint of expensive perfume, made of pure nard, and she anointed Jesus’ feet and wiped them with her hair. And the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
texts.asv: Mary therefore took a pound of ointment of pure nard, very precious, and anointed the feet of Jesus, and wiped his feet with her hair: and the house was filled with the odor of the ointment.

texts.webp: Then Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, one of his disciples, who would betray him, said,
texts.bsb: But one of His disciples, Judas Iscariot, who was going to betray Him, asked,
texts.asv: But Judas Iscariot, one of his disciples, that should betray him, saith,

texts.webp: “Why wasn’t this ointment sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?”
texts.bsb: “Why wasn’t this perfume sold for three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor?”
texts.asv: Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred shillings, and given to the poor?

texts.webp: Now he said this, not because he cared for the poor, but because he was a thief, and having the money box, used to steal what was put into it.
texts.bsb: Judas did not say this because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief. As keeper of the money bag, he used to take from what was put into it.
texts.asv: Now this he said, not because he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and having the bag took away what was put therein.

texts.webp: But Jesus said, “Leave her alone. She has kept this for the day of my burial.
texts.bsb: “Leave her alone,” Jesus replied. “She has kept this perfume in preparation for the day of My burial.
texts.asv: Jesus therefore said, Suffer her to keep it against the day of my burying.

texts.webp: For you always have the poor with you, but you don’t always have me.”
texts.bsb: The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me.”
texts.asv: For the poor ye have always with you; but me ye have not always.

texts.webp: A large crowd therefore of the Jews learned that he was there; and they came, not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead.
texts.bsb: Meanwhile a large crowd of Jews learned that Jesus was there. And they came not only because of Him, but also to see Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.
texts.asv: The common people therefore of the Jews learned that he was there: and they came, not for Jesus’ sake only, but that they might see Lazarus also, whom he had raised from the dead.

texts.webp: But the chief priests conspired to put Lazarus to death also,
texts.bsb: So the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus as well,
texts.asv: But the chief priests took counsel that they might put Lazarus also to death;

texts.webp: because on account of him many of the Jews went away and believed in Jesus.
texts.bsb: for on account of him many of the Jews were deserting them and believing in Jesus.
texts.asv: because that by reason of him many of the Jews went away, and believed on Jesus.

texts.webp: On the next day a great multitude had come to the feast. When they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,
texts.bsb: The next day the great crowd that had come to the feast heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.
texts.asv: On the morrow a great multitude that had come to the feast, when they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,

texts.webp: they took the branches of the palm trees and went out to meet him, and cried out, “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!”
texts.bsb: They took palm branches and went out to meet Him, shouting:
texts.asv: took the branches of the palm trees, and went forth to meet him, and cried out, Hosanna: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord, even the King of Israel.

texts.webp: Jesus, having found a young donkey, sat on it. As it is written,
texts.bsb: Finding a young donkey, Jesus sat on it, as it is written:
texts.asv: And Jesus, having found a young ass, sat thereon; as it is written,

texts.webp: “Don’t be afraid, daughter of Zion. Behold, your King comes, sitting on a donkey’s colt.”
texts.bsb: “Do not be afraid, O Daughter of Zion.
texts.asv: Fear not, daughter of Zion: behold, thy King cometh, sitting on an ass’s colt.

texts.webp: His disciples didn’t understand these things at first, but when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things were written about him, and that they had done these things to him.
texts.bsb: At first His disciples did not understand these things, but after Jesus was glorified they remembered what had been done to Him, and they realized that these very things had also been written about Him.
texts.asv: These things understood not his disciples at the first: but when Jesus was glorified, then remembered they that these things were written of him, and that they had done these things unto him.

texts.webp: The multitude therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead was testifying about it.
texts.bsb: Meanwhile, many people who had been with Jesus when He called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead continued to testify.
texts.asv: The multitude therefore that was with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb, and raised him from the dead, bare witness.

texts.webp: For this cause also the multitude went and met him, because they heard that he had done this sign.
texts.bsb: That is also why the crowd went out to meet Him, because they heard that He had performed this sign.
texts.asv: For this cause also the multitude went and met him, for that they heard that he had done this sign.

texts.webp: The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, “See how you accomplish nothing. Behold, the world has gone after him.”
texts.bsb: Then the Pharisees said to one another, “You can see that this is doing you no good. Look how the whole world has gone after Him!”
texts.asv: The Pharisees therefore said among themselves, Behold how ye prevail nothing; lo, the world is gone after him.

texts.webp: Now there were certain Greeks among those who went up to worship at the feast.
texts.bsb: Now there were some Greeks among those who went up to worship at the feast.
texts.asv: Now there were certain Greeks among those that went up to worship at the feast:

texts.webp: Therefore, these came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”
texts.bsb: They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and requested of him, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”
texts.asv: these therefore came to Philip, who was of Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying, Sir, we would see Jesus.

texts.webp: Philip came and told Andrew, and in turn, Andrew came with Philip, and they told Jesus.
texts.bsb: Philip relayed this appeal to Andrew, and both of them went and told Jesus.
texts.asv: Philip cometh and telleth Andrew: Andrew cometh, and Philip, and they tell Jesus.

texts.webp: Jesus answered them, “The time has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
texts.bsb: But Jesus replied, “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
texts.asv: And Jesus answereth them, saying, The hour is come, that the Son of man should be glorified.

texts.webp: Most certainly I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.
texts.bsb: Truly, truly, I tell you, unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a seed. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.
texts.asv: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a grain of wheat fall into the earth and die, it abideth by itself alone; but if it die, it beareth much fruit.

texts.webp: He who loves his life will lose it. He who hates his life in this world will keep it to eternal life.
texts.bsb: Whoever loves his life will lose it, but whoever hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
texts.asv: He that loveth his life loseth it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal.

texts.webp: If anyone serves me, let him follow me. Where I am, there my servant will also be. If anyone serves me, the Father will honor him.
texts.bsb: If anyone serves Me, he must follow Me; and where I am, My servant will be as well. If anyone serves Me, the Father will honor him.
texts.asv: If any man serve me, let him follow me; and where I am, there shall also my servant be: if any man serve me, him will the Father honor.

texts.webp: “Now my soul is troubled. What shall I say? ‘Father, save me from this time’? But I came to this time for this cause.
texts.bsb: Now My soul is troubled, and what shall I say? ‘Father, save Me from this hour’? No, it is for this purpose that I have come to this hour.
texts.asv: Now is my soul troubled; and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour. But for this cause came I unto this hour.

texts.webp: Father, glorify your name!”
texts.bsb: Father, glorify Your name!”
texts.asv: Father, glorify thy name. There came therefore a voice out of heaven, saying, I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.

texts.webp: Therefore the multitude who stood by and heard it said that it had thundered. Others said, “An angel has spoken to him.”
texts.bsb: The crowd standing there heard it and said that it had thundered. Others said that an angel had spoken to Him.
texts.asv: The multitude therefore, that stood by, and heard it, said that it had thundered: others said, An angel hath spoken to him.

texts.webp: Jesus answered, “This voice hasn’t come for my sake, but for your sakes.
texts.bsb: In response, Jesus said, “This voice was not for My benefit, but yours.
texts.asv: Jesus answered and said, This voice hath not come for my sake, but for your sakes.

texts.webp: Now is the judgment of this world. Now the prince of this world will be cast out.
texts.bsb: Now judgment is upon this world; now the prince of this world will be cast out.
texts.asv: Now is the judgment of this world: now shall the prince of this world be cast out.

texts.webp: And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself.”
texts.bsb: And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw everyone to Myself.”
texts.asv: And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto myself.

texts.webp: But he said this, signifying by what kind of death he should die.
texts.bsb: He said this to indicate the kind of death He was going to die.
texts.asv: But this he said, signifying by what manner of death he should die.

texts.webp: The multitude answered him, “We have heard out of the law that the Christ remains forever. How do you say, ‘The Son of Man must be lifted up’? Who is this Son of Man?”
texts.bsb: The crowd replied, “We have heard from the Law that the Christ will remain forever. So how can You say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”
texts.asv: The multitude therefore answered him, We have heard out of the law that the Christ abideth for ever: and how sayest thou, The Son of man must be lifted up? who is this Son of man?

texts.webp: Jesus therefore said to them, “Yet a little while the light is with you. Walk while you have the light, that darkness doesn’t overtake you. He who walks in the darkness doesn’t know where he is going.
texts.bsb: Then Jesus told them, “For a little while longer, the Light will be among you. Walk while you have the Light, so that darkness will not overtake you. The one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.
texts.asv: Jesus therefore said unto them, Yet a little while is the light among you. Walk while ye have the light, that darkness overtake you not: and he that walketh in the darkness knoweth not whither he goeth.

texts.webp: While you have the light, believe in the light, that you may become children of light.” Jesus said these things, and he departed and hid himself from them.
texts.bsb: While you have the Light, believe in the Light, so that you may become sons of light.”
texts.asv: While ye have the light, believe on the light, that ye may become sons of light.

texts.webp: But though he had done so many signs before them, yet they didn’t believe in him,
texts.bsb: Although Jesus had performed so many signs in their presence, they still did not believe in Him.
texts.asv: But though he had done so many signs before them, yet they believed not on him:

texts.webp: that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spoke:
texts.bsb: This was to fulfill the word of Isaiah the prophet:
texts.asv: that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spake,

texts.webp: For this cause they couldn’t believe, for Isaiah said again:
texts.bsb: For this reason they were unable to believe. For again, Isaiah says:
texts.asv: For this cause they could not believe, for that Isaiah said again,

texts.webp: “He has blinded their eyes and he hardened their heart,
texts.bsb: “He has blinded their eyes
texts.asv: He hath blinded their eyes, and he hardened their heart;

texts.webp: Isaiah said these things when he saw his glory, and spoke of him.
texts.bsb: Isaiah said these things because he saw Jesus’ glory and spoke about Him.
texts.asv: These things said Isaiah, because he saw his glory; and he spake of him.

texts.webp: Nevertheless, even many of the rulers believed in him, but because of the Pharisees they didn’t confess it, so that they wouldn’t be put out of the synagogue,
texts.bsb: Nevertheless, many of the leaders believed in Him. But because of the Pharisees they did not confess Him, for fear that they would be put out of the synagogue.
texts.asv: Nevertheless even of the rulers many believed on him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess it, lest they should be put out of the synagogue:

texts.webp: for they loved men’s praise more than God’s praise.
texts.bsb: For they loved praise from men more than praise from God.
texts.asv: for they loved the glory that is of men more than the glory that is of God.

texts.webp: Jesus cried out and said, “Whoever believes in me, believes not in me, but in him who sent me.
texts.bsb: Then Jesus cried out, “Whoever believes in Me does not believe in Me alone, but in the One who sent Me.
texts.asv: And Jesus cried and said, He that believeth on me, believeth not on me, but on him that sent me.

texts.webp: He who sees me sees him who sent me.
texts.bsb: And whoever sees Me sees the One who sent Me.
texts.asv: And he that beholdeth me beholdeth him that sent me.

texts.webp: I have come as a light into the world, that whoever believes in me may not remain in the darkness.
texts.bsb: I have come into the world as a light, so that no one who believes in Me should remain in darkness.
texts.asv: I am come a light into the world, that whosoever believeth on me may not abide in the darkness.

texts.webp: If anyone listens to my sayings and doesn’t believe, I don’t judge him. For I came not to judge the world, but to save the world.
texts.bsb: As for anyone who hears My words and does not keep them, I do not judge him. For I have not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
texts.asv: And if any man hear my sayings, and keep them not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world.

texts.webp: He who rejects me, and doesn’t receive my sayings, has one who judges him. The word that I spoke will judge him in the last day.
texts.bsb: There is a judge for the one who rejects Me and does not receive My words: The word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day.
texts.asv: He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my sayings, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I spake, the same shall judge him in the last day.

texts.webp: For I spoke not from myself, but the Father who sent me gave me a commandment, what I should say and what I should speak.
texts.bsb: I have not spoken on My own, but the Father who sent Me has commanded Me what to say and how to say it.
texts.asv: For I spake not from myself; but the Father that sent me, he hath given me a commandment, what I should say, and what I should speak.

texts.webp: I know that his commandment is eternal life. The things therefore which I speak, even as the Father has said to me, so I speak.”
texts.bsb: And I know that His command leads to eternal life. So I speak exactly what the Father has told Me to say.”
texts.asv: And I know that his commandment is life eternal; the things therefore which I speak, even as the Father hath said unto me, so I speak.

texts.webp: Now before the feast of the Passover, Jesus, knowing that his time had come that he would depart from this world to the Father, having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the end.
texts.bsb: It was now just before the Passover Feast, and Jesus knew that His hour had come to leave this world and return to the Father. Having loved His own who were in the world, He loved them to the very end.
texts.asv: Now before the feast of the passover, Jesus knowing that his hour was come that he should depart out of this world unto the Father, having loved his own that were in the world, he loved them unto the end.

texts.webp: During supper, the devil having already put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him,
texts.bsb: The evening meal was underway, and the devil had already put into the heart of Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot, to betray Jesus.
texts.asv: And during supper, the devil having already put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him,

texts.webp: Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he came from God and was going to God,
texts.bsb: Jesus knew that the Father had delivered all things into His hands, and that He had come from God and was returning to God.
texts.asv: Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he came forth from God, and goeth unto God,

texts.webp: arose from supper, and laid aside his outer garments. He took a towel and wrapped a towel around his waist.
texts.bsb: So He got up from the supper, laid aside His outer garments, and wrapped a towel around His waist.
texts.asv: riseth from supper, and layeth aside his garments; and he took a towel, and girded himself.

texts.webp: Then he poured water into the basin, and began to wash the disciples’ feet and to wipe them with the towel that was wrapped around him.
texts.bsb: After that, He poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples’ feet and dry them with the towel that was around Him.
texts.asv: Then he poureth water into the basin, and began to wash the disciples’ feet, and to wipe them with the towel wherewith he was girded.

texts.webp: Then he came to Simon Peter. He said to him, “Lord, do you wash my feet?”
texts.bsb: He came to Simon Peter, who asked Him, “Lord, are You going to wash my feet?”
texts.asv: So he cometh to Simon Peter. He saith unto him, Lord, dost thou wash my feet?

texts.webp: Jesus answered him, “You don’t know what I am doing now, but you will understand later.”
texts.bsb: Jesus replied, “You do not realize now what I am doing, but later you will understand.”
texts.asv: Jesus answered and said unto him, What I do thou knowest not now; but thou shalt understand hereafter.

texts.webp: Peter said to him, “You will never wash my feet!”
texts.bsb: “Never shall You wash my feet!” Peter told Him.
texts.asv: Peter saith unto him, Thou shalt never wash my feet. Jesus answered him, If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me.

texts.webp: Simon Peter said to him, “Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head!”
texts.bsb: “Then, Lord,” Simon Peter replied, “not only my feet, but my hands and my head as well!”
texts.asv: Simon Peter saith unto him, Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head.

texts.webp: Jesus said to him, “Someone who has bathed only needs to have his feet washed, but is completely clean. You are clean, but not all of you.”
texts.bsb: Jesus told him, “Whoever has already bathed needs only to wash his feet, and he will be completely clean. And you are clean, though not all of you.”
texts.asv: Jesus saith to him, He that is bathed needeth not save to wash his feet, but is clean every whit: and ye are clean, but not all.

texts.webp: For he knew him who would betray him; therefore he said, “You are not all clean.”
texts.bsb: For He knew who would betray Him. That is why He said, “Not all of you are clean.”
texts.asv: For he knew him that should betray him; therefore said he, Ye are not all clean.

texts.webp: So when he had washed their feet, put his outer garment back on, and sat down again, he said to them, “Do you know what I have done to you?
texts.bsb: When Jesus had washed their feet and put on His outer garments, He reclined with them again and asked, “Do you know what I have done for you?
texts.asv: So when he had washed their feet, and taken his garments, and sat down again, he said unto them, Know ye what I have done to you?

texts.webp: You call me, ‘Teacher’ and ‘Lord.’ You say so correctly, for so I am.
texts.bsb: You call Me Teacher and Lord, and rightly so, because I am.
texts.asv: Ye call me, Teacher, and, Lord: and ye say well; for so I am.

texts.webp: If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet.
texts.bsb: So if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also should wash one another’s feet.
texts.asv: If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, ye also ought to wash one another’s feet.

texts.webp: For I have given you an example, that you should also do as I have done to you.
texts.bsb: I have set you an example so that you should do as I have done for you.
texts.asv: For I have given you an example, that ye also should do as I have done to you.

texts.webp: Most certainly I tell you, a servant is not greater than his lord, neither is one who is sent greater than he who sent him.
texts.bsb: Truly, truly, I tell you, no servant is greater than his master, nor is a messenger greater than the one who sent him.
texts.asv: Verily, verily, I say unto you, A servant is not greater than his lord; neither one that is sent greater than he that sent him.

texts.webp: If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.
texts.bsb: If you know these things, you will be blessed if you do them.
texts.asv: If ye know these things, blessed are ye if ye do them.

texts.webp: I don’t speak concerning all of you. I know whom I have chosen; but that the Scripture may be fulfilled, ‘He who eats bread with me has lifted up his heel against me.’
texts.bsb: I am not speaking about all of you; I know whom I have chosen. But this is to fulfill the Scripture: ‘The one who shares My bread has lifted up his heel against Me.’
texts.asv: I speak not of you all: I know whom I have chosen: but that the scripture may be fulfilled, He that eateth my bread lifted up his heel against me.

texts.webp: From now on, I tell you before it happens, that when it happens, you may believe that I am he.
texts.bsb: I am telling you now before it happens, so that when it comes to pass, you will believe that I am He.
texts.asv: From henceforth I tell you before it come to pass, that, when it is come to pass, ye may believe that I am he.

texts.webp: Most certainly I tell you, he who receives whomever I send, receives me; and he who receives me, receives him who sent me.”
texts.bsb: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever receives the one I send receives Me, and whoever receives Me receives the One who sent Me.”
texts.asv: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.

texts.webp: When Jesus had said this, he was troubled in spirit, and testified, “Most certainly I tell you that one of you will betray me.”
texts.bsb: After Jesus had said this, He became troubled in spirit and testified, “Truly, truly, I tell you, one of you will betray Me.”
texts.asv: When Jesus had thus said, he was troubled in the spirit, and testified, and said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.

texts.webp: The disciples looked at one another, perplexed about whom he spoke.
texts.bsb: The disciples looked at one another, perplexed as to which of them He meant.
texts.asv: The disciples looked one on another, doubting of whom he spake.

texts.webp: One of his disciples, whom Jesus loved, was at the table, leaning against Jesus’ chest.
texts.bsb: One of His disciples, the one whom Jesus loved, was reclining at His side.
texts.asv: There was at the table reclining in Jesus’ bosom one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved.

texts.webp: Simon Peter therefore beckoned to him, and said to him, “Tell us who it is of whom he speaks.”
texts.bsb: So Simon Peter motioned to him to ask Jesus which one He was talking about.
texts.asv: Simon Peter therefore beckoneth to him, and saith unto him, Tell us who it is of whom he speaketh.

texts.webp: He, leaning back, as he was, on Jesus’ chest, asked him, “Lord, who is it?”
texts.bsb: Leaning back against Jesus, he asked, “Lord, who is it?”
texts.asv: He leaning back, as he was, on Jesus’ breast saith unto him, Lord, who is it?

texts.webp: Jesus therefore answered, “It is he to whom I will give this piece of bread when I have dipped it.” So when he had dipped the piece of bread, he gave it to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot.
texts.bsb: Jesus answered, “It is the one to whom I give this morsel after I have dipped it.” Then He dipped the morsel and gave it to Judas son of Simon Iscariot.
texts.asv: Jesus therefore answereth, He it is, for whom I shall dip the sop, and give it him. So when he had dipped the sop, he taketh and giveth it to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot.

texts.webp: After the piece of bread, then Satan entered into him.
texts.bsb: And when Judas had taken the morsel, Satan entered into him.
texts.asv: And after the sop, then entered Satan into him. Jesus therefore saith unto him, What thou doest, do quickly.

texts.webp: Now nobody at the table knew why he said this to him.
texts.bsb: But no one at the table knew why Jesus had said this to him.
texts.asv: Now no man at the table knew for what intent he spake this unto him.

texts.webp: For some thought, because Judas had the money box, that Jesus said to him, “Buy what things we need for the feast,” or that he should give something to the poor.
texts.bsb: Since Judas kept the money bag, some thought that Jesus was telling him to buy what was needed for the feast, or to give something to the poor.
texts.asv: For some thought, because Judas had the bag, that Jesus said unto him, Buy what things we have need of for the feast; or, that he should give something to the poor.

texts.webp: Therefore having received that morsel, he went out immediately. It was night.
texts.bsb: As soon as he had received the morsel, Judas went out into the night.
texts.asv: He then having received the sop went out straightway: and it was night.

texts.webp: When he had gone out, Jesus said, “Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God has been glorified in him.
texts.bsb: When Judas had gone out, Jesus said, “Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in Him.
texts.asv: When therefore he was gone out, Jesus saith, Now is the Son of man glorified, and God is glorified in him;

texts.webp: If God has been glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and he will glorify him immediately.
texts.bsb: If God is glorified in Him, God will also glorify the Son in Himself — and will glorify Him at once.
texts.asv: and God shall glorify him in himself, and straightway shall he glorify him.

texts.webp: Little children, I will be with you a little while longer. You will seek me, and as I said to the Jews, ‘Where I am going, you can’t come,’ so now I tell you.
texts.bsb: Little children, I am with you only a little while longer. You will look for Me, and as I said to the Jews, so now I say to you: ‘Where I am going, you cannot come.’
texts.asv: Little children, yet a little while I am with you. Ye shall seek me: and as I said unto the Jews, Whither I go, ye cannot come; so now I say unto you.

texts.webp: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.
texts.bsb: A new commandment I give you: Love one another. As I have loved you, so you also must love one another.
texts.asv: A new commandment I give unto you, that ye love one another; even as I have loved you, that ye also love one another.

texts.webp: By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.”
texts.bsb: By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you love one another.”
texts.asv: By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.

texts.webp: Simon Peter said to him, “Lord, where are you going?”
texts.bsb: “Lord, where are You going?” Simon Peter asked.
texts.asv: Simon Peter saith unto him, Lord, whither goest thou? Jesus answered, Whither I go, thou canst not follow me now; but thou shalt follow afterwards.

texts.webp: Peter said to him, “Lord, why can’t I follow you now? I will lay down my life for you.”
texts.bsb: “Lord,” said Peter, “why can’t I follow You now? I will lay down my life for You.”
texts.asv: Peter saith unto him, Lord, why cannot I follow thee even now? I will lay down my life for thee.

texts.webp: Jesus answered him, “Will you lay down your life for me? Most certainly I tell you, the rooster won’t crow until you have denied me three times.
texts.bsb: “Will you lay down your life for Me?” Jesus replied. “Truly, truly, I tell you, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times.[’’]
texts.asv: Jesus answereth, Wilt thou lay down thy life for me? Verily, verily, I say unto thee, The cock shall not crow, till thou hast denied me thrice.

texts.webp: “Don’t let your heart be troubled. Believe in God. Believe also in me.
texts.bsb: “Do not let your hearts be troubled. You believe in God; believe in Me as well.
texts.asv: Let not your heart be troubled: believe in God, believe also in me.

texts.webp: In my Father’s house are many homes. If it weren’t so, I would have told you. I am going to prepare a place for you.
texts.bsb: In My Father’s house are many rooms. If it were not so, would I have told you that I am going there to prepare a place for you?
texts.asv: In my Father’s house are many mansions; if it were not so, I would have told you; for I go to prepare a place for you.

texts.webp: If I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and will receive you to myself; that where I am, you may be there also.
texts.bsb: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come back and welcome you into My presence, so that you also may be where I am.
texts.asv: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I come again, and will receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.

texts.webp: You know where I go, and you know the way.”
texts.bsb: You know the way to the place where I am going. ”
texts.asv: And whither I go, ye know the way.

texts.webp: Thomas said to him, “Lord, we don’t know where you are going. How can we know the way?”
texts.bsb: “Lord,” said Thomas, “we do not know where You are going, so how can we know the way?”
texts.asv: Thomas saith unto him, Lord, we know not whither thou goest; how know we the way?

texts.webp: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father, except through me.
texts.bsb: Jesus answered, “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
texts.asv: Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, and the truth, and the life: no one cometh unto the Father, but by me.

texts.webp: If you had known me, you would have known my Father also. From now on, you know him and have seen him.”
texts.bsb: If you had known Me, you would know My Father as well. From now on you do know Him and have seen Him.”
texts.asv: If ye had known me, ye would have known my Father also: from henceforth ye know him, and have seen him.

texts.webp: Philip said to him, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.”
texts.bsb: Philip said to Him, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.”
texts.asv: Philip saith unto him, Lord, show us the Father, and it sufficeth us.

texts.webp: Jesus said to him, “Have I been with you such a long time, and do you not know me, Philip? He who has seen me has seen the Father. How do you say, ‘Show us the Father’?
texts.bsb: Jesus replied, “Philip, I have been with you all this time, and still you do not know Me? Anyone who has seen Me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?
texts.asv: Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and dost thou not know me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; how sayest thou, Show us the Father?

texts.webp: Don’t you believe that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? The words that I tell you, I speak not from myself; but the Father who lives in me does his works.
texts.bsb: Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me? The words I say to you, I do not speak on My own. Instead, it is the Father dwelling in Me, performing His works.
texts.asv: Believest thou not that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? the words that I say unto you I speak not from myself: but the Father abiding in me doeth his works.

texts.webp: Believe me that I am in the Father, and the Father in me; or else believe me for the very works’ sake.
texts.bsb: Believe Me that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me — or at least believe on account of the works themselves.
texts.asv: Believe me that I am in the Father, and the Father in me: or else believe me for the very works’ sake.

texts.webp: Most certainly I tell you, he who believes in me, the works that I do, he will do also; and he will do greater works than these, because I am going to my Father.
texts.bsb: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever believes in Me will also do the works that I am doing. He will do even greater things than these, because I am going to the Father.
texts.asv: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto the Father.

texts.webp: Whatever you will ask in my name, I will do it, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
texts.bsb: And I will do whatever you ask in My name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
texts.asv: And whatsoever ye shall ask in my name, that will I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.

texts.webp: If you will ask anything in my name, I will do it.
texts.bsb: If you ask Me for anything in My name, I will do it.
texts.asv: If ye shall ask anything in my name, that will I do.

texts.webp: If you love me, keep my commandments.
texts.bsb: If you love Me, you will keep My commandments.
texts.asv: If ye love me, ye will keep my commandments.

texts.webp: I will pray to the Father, and he will give you another Counselor, that he may be with you forever:
texts.bsb: And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate to be with you forever —
texts.asv: And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may be with you for ever,

texts.webp: the Spirit of truth, whom the world can’t receive, for it doesn’t see him and doesn’t know him. You know him, for he lives with you and will be in you.
texts.bsb: the Spirit of truth. The world cannot receive Him, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him. But you do know Him, for He abides with you and will be in you.
texts.asv: even the Spirit of truth: whom the world cannot receive; for it beholdeth him not, neither knoweth him: ye know him; for he abideth with you, and shall be in you.

texts.webp: I will not leave you orphans. I will come to you.
texts.bsb: I will not leave you as orphans; I will come to you.
texts.asv: I will not leave you desolate: I come unto you.

texts.webp: Yet a little while, and the world will see me no more; but you will see me. Because I live, you will live also.
texts.bsb: In a little while the world will see Me no more, but you will see Me. Because I live, you also will live.
texts.asv: Yet a little while, and the world beholdeth me no more; but ye behold me: because I live, ye shall live also.

texts.webp: In that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.
texts.bsb: On that day you will know that I am in My Father, and you are in Me, and I am in you.
texts.asv: In that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you.

texts.webp: One who has my commandments and keeps them, that person is one who loves me. One who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him, and will reveal myself to him.”
texts.bsb: Whoever has My commandments and keeps them is the one who loves Me. The one who loves Me will be loved by My Father, and I will love him and reveal Myself to him.”
texts.asv: He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me: and he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself unto him.

texts.webp: Judas (not Iscariot) said to him, “Lord, what has happened that you are about to reveal yourself to us, and not to the world?”
texts.bsb: Judas (not Iscariot) asked Him, “Lord, why are You going to reveal Yourself to us and not to the world?”
texts.asv: Judas (not Iscariot) saith unto him, Lord, what is come to pass that thou wilt manifest thyself unto us, and not unto the world?

texts.webp: Jesus answered him, “If a man loves me, he will keep my word. My Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him.
texts.bsb: Jesus replied, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word. My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our home with him.
texts.asv: Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love me, he will keep my word: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him.

texts.webp: He who doesn’t love me doesn’t keep my words. The word which you hear isn’t mine, but the Father’s who sent me.
texts.bsb: Whoever does not love Me does not keep My words. The word that you hear is not My own, but it is from the Father who sent Me.
texts.asv: He that loveth me not keepeth not my words: and the word which ye hear is not mine, but the Father’s who sent me.

texts.webp: “I have said these things to you while still living with you.
texts.bsb: All this I have spoken to you while I am still with you.
texts.asv: These things have I spoken unto you, while yet abiding with you.

texts.webp: But the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things, and will remind you of all that I said to you.
texts.bsb: But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in My name, will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have told you.
texts.asv: But the Comforter, even the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring to your remembrance all that I said unto you.

texts.webp: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.
texts.bsb: Peace I leave with you; My peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled; do not be afraid.
texts.asv: Peace I leave with you; my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.

texts.webp: You heard how I told you, ‘I am going away, and I will come back to you.’ If you loved me, you would have rejoiced because I said ‘I am going to my Father;’ for the Father is greater than I.
texts.bsb: You heard Me say, ‘I am going away, and I am coming back to you.’ If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I.
texts.asv: Ye heard how I said to you, I go away, and I come unto you. If ye loved me, ye would have rejoiced, because I go unto the Father: for the Father is greater than I.

texts.webp: Now I have told you before it happens so that when it happens, you may believe.
texts.bsb: And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it does happen, you will believe.
texts.asv: And now I have told you before it come to pass, that, when it is come to pass, ye may believe.

texts.webp: I will no more speak much with you, for the prince of the world comes, and he has nothing in me.
texts.bsb: I will not speak with you much longer, for the prince of this world is coming, and he has no claim on Me.
texts.asv: I will no more speak much with you, for the prince of the world cometh: and he hath nothing in me;

texts.webp: But that the world may know that I love the Father, and as the Father commanded me, even so I do. Arise, let’s go from here.
texts.bsb: But I do exactly what the Father has commanded Me, so that the world may know that I love the Father.
texts.asv: but that the world may know that I love the Father, and as the Father gave me commandment, even so I do. Arise, let us go hence.

texts.webp: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the farmer.
texts.bsb: “I am the true vine, and My Father is the keeper of the vineyard.
texts.asv: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.

texts.webp: Every branch in me that doesn’t bear fruit, he takes away. Every branch that bears fruit, he prunes, that it may bear more fruit.
texts.bsb: He cuts off every branch in Me that bears no fruit, and every branch that does bear fruit, He prunes to make it even more fruitful.
texts.asv: Every branch in me that beareth not fruit, he taketh it away: and every branch that beareth fruit, he cleanseth it, that it may bear more fruit.

texts.webp: You are already pruned clean because of the word which I have spoken to you.
texts.bsb: You are already clean because of the word I have spoken to you.
texts.asv: Already ye are clean because of the word which I have spoken unto you.

texts.webp: Remain in me, and I in you. As the branch can’t bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you, unless you remain in me.
texts.bsb: Remain in Me, and I will remain in you. Just as no branch can bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in Me.
texts.asv: Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; so neither can ye, except ye abide in me.

texts.webp: I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.
texts.bsb: I am the vine and you are the branches. The one who remains in Me, and I in him, will bear much fruit. For apart from Me you can do nothing.
texts.asv: I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same beareth much fruit: for apart from me ye can do nothing.

texts.webp: If a man doesn’t remain in me, he is thrown out as a branch and is withered; and they gather them, throw them into the fire, and they are burned.
texts.bsb: If anyone does not remain in Me, he is like a branch that is thrown away and withers. Such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire, and burned.
texts.asv: If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and they gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned.

texts.webp: If you remain in me, and my words remain in you, you will ask whatever you desire, and it will be done for you.
texts.bsb: If you remain in Me and My words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.
texts.asv: If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ask whatsoever ye will, and it shall be done unto you.

texts.webp: “In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit; and so you will be my disciples.
texts.bsb: This is to My Father’s glory, that you bear much fruit, proving yourselves to be My disciples.
texts.asv: Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; and so shall ye be my disciples.

texts.webp: Even as the Father has loved me, I also have loved you. Remain in my love.
texts.bsb: As the Father has loved Me, so have I loved you. Remain in My love.
texts.asv: Even as the Father hath loved me, I also have loved you: abide ye in my love.

texts.webp: If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, even as I have kept my Father’s commandments and remain in his love.
texts.bsb: If you keep My commandments, you will remain in My love, just as I have kept My Father’s commandments and remain in His love.
texts.asv: If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and abide in his love.

texts.webp: I have spoken these things to you, that my joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be made full.
texts.bsb: I have told you these things so that My joy may be in you and your joy may be complete.
texts.asv: These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be made full.

texts.webp: “This is my commandment, that you love one another, even as I have loved you.
texts.bsb: This is My commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.
texts.asv: This is my commandment, that ye love one another, even as I have loved you.

texts.webp: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.
texts.bsb: Greater love has no one than this, that he lay down his life for his friends.
texts.asv: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.

texts.webp: You are my friends if you do whatever I command you.
texts.bsb: You are My friends if you do what I command you.
texts.asv: Ye are my friends, if ye do the things which I command you.

texts.webp: No longer do I call you servants, for the servant doesn’t know what his lord does. But I have called you friends, for everything that I heard from my Father, I have made known to you.
texts.bsb: No longer do I call you servants, for a servant does not understand what his master is doing. But I have called you friends, because everything I have learned from My Father I have made known to you.
texts.asv: No longer do I call you servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I heard from my Father I have made known unto you.

texts.webp: You didn’t choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain; that whatever you will ask of the Father in my name, he may give it to you.
texts.bsb: You did not choose Me, but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit — fruit that will remain — so that whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.
texts.asv: Ye did not choose me, but I chose you, and appointed you, that ye should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should abide: that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you.

texts.webp: “I command these things to you, that you may love one another.
texts.bsb: This is My command to you: Love one another.
texts.asv: These things I command you, that ye may love one another.

texts.webp: If the world hates you, you know that it has hated me before it hated you.
texts.bsb: If the world hates you, understand that it hated Me first.
texts.asv: If the world hateth you, ye know that it hath hated me before it hated you.

texts.webp: If you were of the world, the world would love its own. But because you are not of the world, since I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you.
texts.bsb: If you were of the world, it would love you as its own. Instead, the world hates you, because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world.
texts.asv: If ye were of the world, the world would love its own: but because ye are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you.

texts.webp: Remember the word that I said to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his lord.’ If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you. If they kept my word, they will also keep yours.
texts.bsb: Remember the word that I spoke to you: ‘No servant is greater than his master.’ If they persecuted Me, they will persecute you as well; if they kept My word, they will keep yours as well.
texts.asv: Remember the word that I said unto you, A servant is not greater than his lord. If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they kept my word, they will keep yours also.

texts.webp: But they will do all these things to you for my name’s sake, because they don’t know him who sent me.
texts.bsb: But they will treat you like this because of My name, since they do not know the One who sent Me.
texts.asv: But all these things will they do unto you for my name’s sake, because they know not him that sent me.

texts.webp: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have had sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.
texts.bsb: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not be guilty of sin. Now, however, they have no excuse for their sin.
texts.asv: If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no excuse for their sin.

texts.webp: He who hates me, hates my Father also.
texts.bsb: Whoever hates Me hates My Father as well.
texts.asv: He that hateth me hateth my Father also.

texts.webp: If I hadn’t done among them the works which no one else did, they wouldn’t have had sin. But now they have seen and also hated both me and my Father.
texts.bsb: If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would not be guilty of sin; but now they have seen and hated both Me and My Father.
texts.asv: If I had not done among them the works which none other did, they had not had sin: but now have they both seen and hated both me and my Father.

texts.webp: But this happened so that the word may be fulfilled which was written in their law, ‘They hated me without a cause.’
texts.bsb: But this is to fulfill what is written in their Law: ‘They hated Me without reason.’
texts.asv: But this cometh to pass, that the word may be fulfilled that is written in their law, They hated me without a cause.

texts.webp: “When the Counselor has come, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will testify about me.
texts.bsb: When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father — the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father — He will testify about Me.
texts.asv: But when the Comforter is come, whom I will send unto you from the Father, even the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father, he shall bear witness of me:

texts.webp: You will also testify, because you have been with me from the beginning.
texts.bsb: And you also must testify, because you have been with Me from the beginning.[’’]
texts.asv: and ye also bear witness, because ye have been with me from the beginning.

texts.webp: “I have said these things to you so that you wouldn’t be caused to stumble.
texts.bsb: “I have told you these things so that you will not fall away.
texts.asv: These things have I spoken unto you, that ye should not be caused to stumble.

texts.webp: They will put you out of the synagogues. Yes, the time is coming that whoever kills you will think that he offers service to God.
texts.bsb: They will put you out of the synagogues. In fact, a time is coming when anyone who kills you will think he is offering a service to God.
texts.asv: They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the hour cometh, that whosoever killeth you shall think that he offereth service unto God.

texts.webp: They will do these things because they have not known the Father nor me.
texts.bsb: They will do these things because they have not known the Father or Me.
texts.asv: And these things will they do, because they have not known the Father, nor me.

texts.webp: But I have told you these things so that when the time comes, you may remember that I told you about them. I didn’t tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you.
texts.bsb: But I have told you these things so that when their hour comes, you will remember that I told you about them. I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you.
texts.asv: But these things have I spoken unto you, that when their hour is come, ye may remember them, how that I told you. And these things I said not unto you from the beginning, because I was with you.

texts.webp: But now I am going to him who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’
texts.bsb: Now, however, I am going to Him who sent Me; yet none of you asks Me, ‘Where are You going?’
texts.asv: But now I go unto him that sent me; and none of you asketh me, Whither goest thou?

texts.webp: But because I have told you these things, sorrow has filled your heart.
texts.bsb: Instead, your hearts are filled with sorrow because I have told you these things.
texts.asv: But because I have spoken these things unto you, sorrow hath filled your heart.

texts.webp: Nevertheless I tell you the truth: It is to your advantage that I go away; for if I don’t go away, the Counselor won’t come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you.
texts.bsb: But I tell you the truth, it is for your benefit that I am going away. Unless I go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send Him to you.
texts.asv: Nevertheless I tell you the truth: It is expedient for you that I go away; for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I go, I will send him unto you.

texts.webp: When he has come, he will convict the world about sin, about righteousness, and about judgment;
texts.bsb: And when He comes, He will convict the world in regard to sin and righteousness and judgment:
texts.asv: And he, when he is come, will convict the world in respect of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment:

texts.webp: about sin, because they don’t believe in me;
texts.bsb: in regard to sin, because they do not believe in Me;
texts.asv: of sin, because they believe not on me;

texts.webp: about righteousness, because I am going to my Father, and you won’t see me any more;
texts.bsb: in regard to righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you will no longer see Me;
texts.asv: of righteousness, because I go to the Father, and ye behold me no more;

texts.webp: about judgment, because the prince of this world has been judged.
texts.bsb: and in regard to judgment, because the prince of this world has been condemned.
texts.asv: of judgment, because the prince of this world hath been judged.

texts.webp: “I still have many things to tell you, but you can’t bear them now.
texts.bsb: I still have much to tell you, but you cannot yet bear to hear it.
texts.asv: I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.

texts.webp: However, when he, the Spirit of truth, has come, he will guide you into all truth, for he will not speak from himself; but whatever he hears, he will speak. He will declare to you things that are coming.
texts.bsb: However, when the Spirit of truth comes, He will guide you into all truth. For He will not speak on His own, but He will speak what He hears, and He will declare to you what is to come.
texts.asv: Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he shall guide you into all the truth: for he shall not speak from himself; but what things soever he shall hear, these shall he speak: and he shall declare unto you the things that are to come.

texts.webp: He will glorify me, for he will take from what is mine and will declare it to you.
texts.bsb: He will glorify Me by taking from what is Mine and disclosing it to you.
texts.asv: He shall glorify me: for he shall take of mine, and shall declare it unto you.

texts.webp: All things that the Father has are mine; therefore I said that he takes of mine and will declare it to you.
texts.bsb: Everything that belongs to the Father is Mine. That is why I said that the Spirit will take from what is Mine and disclose it to you.
texts.asv: All things whatsoever the Father hath are mine: therefore said I, that he taketh of mine, and shall declare it unto you.

texts.webp: “A little while, and you will not see me. Again a little while, and you will see me.”
texts.bsb: In a little while you will see Me no more, and then after a little while you will see Me. ”
texts.asv: A little while, and ye behold me no more; and again a little while, and ye shall see me.
