texts.webp: Some of his disciples therefore said to one another, “What is this that he says to us, ‘A little while, and you won’t see me, and again a little while, and you will see me;’ and, ‘Because I go to the Father’?”
texts.bsb: Then some of His disciples asked one another, “Why is He telling us, ‘In a little while you will not see Me, and then after a little while you will see Me’ and ‘Because I am going to the Father’?”
texts.asv: Some of his disciples therefore said one to another, What is this that he saith unto us, A little while, and ye behold me not; and again a little while, and ye shall see me: and, Because I go to the Father?

texts.webp: They said therefore, “What is this that he says, ‘A little while’? We don’t know what he is saying.”
texts.bsb: They kept asking, “Why is He saying, ‘a little while’? We do not understand what He is saying.”
texts.asv: They said therefore, What is this that he saith, A little while? We know not what he saith.

texts.webp: Therefore Jesus perceived that they wanted to ask him, and he said to them, “Do you inquire among yourselves concerning this, that I said, ‘A little while, and you won’t see me, and again a little while, and you will see me’?
texts.bsb: Aware that they wanted to question Him, Jesus said to them, “Are you asking one another why I said, ‘In a little while you will not see Me, and then after a little while you will see Me’?
texts.asv: Jesus perceived that they were desirous to ask him, and he said unto them, Do ye inquire among yourselves concerning this, that I said, A little while, and ye behold me not, and again a little while, and ye shall see me?

texts.webp: Most certainly I tell you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy.
texts.bsb: Truly, truly, I tell you, you will weep and wail while the world rejoices. You will grieve, but your grief will turn to joy.
texts.asv: Verily, verily, I say unto you, that ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy.

texts.webp: A woman, when she gives birth, has sorrow because her time has come. But when she has delivered the child, she doesn’t remember the anguish any more, for the joy that a human being is born into the world.
texts.bsb: A woman has pain in childbirth because her time has come; but when she brings forth her child, she forgets her anguish because of her joy that a child has been born into the world.
texts.asv: A woman when she is in travail hath sorrow, because her hour is come: but when she is delivered of the child, she remembereth no more the anguish, for the joy that a man is born into the world.

texts.webp: Therefore you now have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy away from you.
texts.bsb: So also you have sorrow now, but I will see you again and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take away your joy.
texts.asv: And ye therefore now have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no one taketh away from you.

texts.webp: “In that day you will ask me no questions. Most certainly I tell you, whatever you may ask of the Father in my name, he will give it to you.
texts.bsb: In that day you will no longer ask Me anything. Truly, truly, I tell you, whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.
texts.asv: And in that day ye shall ask me no question. Verily, verily, I say unto you, If ye shall ask anything of the Father, he will give it you in my name.

texts.webp: Until now, you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be made full.
texts.bsb: Until now you have not asked for anything in My name. Ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.
texts.asv: Hitherto have ye asked nothing in my name: ask, and ye shall receive, that your joy may be made full.

texts.webp: “I have spoken these things to you in figures of speech. But the time is coming when I will no more speak to you in figures of speech, but will tell you plainly about the Father.
texts.bsb: I have spoken these things to you in figures of speech. An hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you this way, but will tell you plainly about the Father.
texts.asv: These things have I spoken unto you in dark sayings: the hour cometh, when I shall no more speak unto you in dark sayings, but shall tell you plainly of the Father.

texts.webp: In that day you will ask in my name; and I don’t say to you that I will pray to the Father for you,
texts.bsb: In that day you will ask in My name. I am not saying that I will ask the Father on your behalf.
texts.asv: In that day ye shall ask in my name: and I say not unto you, that I will pray the Father for you;

texts.webp: for the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me, and have believed that I came from God.
texts.bsb: For the Father Himself loves you, because you have loved Me and have believed that I came from God.
texts.asv: for the Father himself loveth you, because ye have loved me, and have believed that I came forth from the Father.

texts.webp: I came from the Father and have come into the world. Again, I leave the world and go to the Father.”
texts.bsb: I came from the Father and entered the world. In turn, I will leave the world and go to the Father.”
texts.asv: I came out from the Father, and am come into the world: again, I leave the world, and go unto the Father.

texts.webp: His disciples said to him, “Behold, now you are speaking plainly, and using no figures of speech.
texts.bsb: His disciples said, “See, now You are speaking plainly and without figures of speech.
texts.asv: His disciples say, Lo, now speakest thou plainly, and speakest no dark saying.

texts.webp: Now we know that you know all things, and don’t need for anyone to question you. By this we believe that you came from God.”
texts.bsb: Now we understand that You know all things and that You have no need for anyone to question You. Because of this, we believe that You came from God.”
texts.asv: Now know we that thou knowest all things, and needest not that any man should ask thee: by this we believe that thou camest forth from God.

texts.webp: Jesus answered them, “Do you now believe?
texts.bsb: “Do you finally believe?” Jesus replied.
texts.asv: Jesus answered them, Do ye now believe?

texts.webp: Behold, the time is coming, yes, and has now come, that you will be scattered, everyone to his own place, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
texts.bsb: “Look, an hour is coming and has already come when you will be scattered, each to his own home, and you will leave Me all alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with Me.
texts.asv: Behold, the hour cometh, yea, is come, that ye shall be scattered, every man to his own, and shall leave me alone: and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.

texts.webp: I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.”
texts.bsb: I have told you these things so that in Me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation. But take courage; I have overcome the world!”
texts.asv: These things have I spoken unto you, that in me ye may have peace. In the world ye have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.

texts.webp: Jesus said these things, then lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said, “Father, the time has come. Glorify your Son, that your Son may also glorify you;
texts.bsb: When Jesus had spoken these things, He lifted up His eyes to heaven and said, “Father, the hour has come. Glorify Your Son, that Your Son may glorify You.
texts.asv: These things spake Jesus; and lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said, Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that the Son may glorify thee:

texts.webp: even as you gave him authority over all flesh, so he will give eternal life to all whom you have given him.
texts.bsb: For You granted Him authority over all people, so that He may give eternal life to all those You have given Him.
texts.asv: even as thou gavest him authority over all flesh, that to all whom thou hast given him, he should give eternal life.

texts.webp: This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ.
texts.bsb: Now this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.
texts.asv: And this is life eternal, that they should know thee the only true God, and him whom thou didst send, even Jesus Christ.

texts.webp: I glorified you on the earth. I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do.
texts.bsb: I have glorified You on earth by accomplishing the work You gave Me to do.
texts.asv: I glorified thee on the earth, having accomplished the work which thou hast given me to do.

texts.webp: Now, Father, glorify me with your own self with the glory which I had with you before the world existed.
texts.bsb: And now, Father, glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.
texts.asv: And now, Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.

texts.webp: “I revealed your name to the people whom you have given me out of the world. They were yours, and you have given them to me. They have kept your word.
texts.bsb: I have revealed Your name to those You have given Me out of the world. They were Yours; You gave them to Me, and they have kept Your word.
texts.asv: I manifested thy name unto the men whom thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them to me; and they have kept thy word.

texts.webp: Now they have known that all things whatever you have given me are from you,
texts.bsb: Now they know that everything You have given Me comes from You.
texts.asv: Now they know that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are from thee:

texts.webp: for the words which you have given me I have given to them; and they received them, and knew for sure that I came from you. They have believed that you sent me.
texts.bsb: For I have given them the words You gave Me, and they have received them. They knew with certainty that I came from You, and they believed that You sent Me.
texts.asv: for the words which thou gavest me I have given unto them; and they received them, and knew of a truth that I came forth from thee, and they believed that thou didst send me.

texts.webp: I pray for them. I don’t pray for the world, but for those whom you have given me, for they are yours.
texts.bsb: I ask on their behalf. I do not ask on behalf of the world, but on behalf of those You have given Me; for they are Yours.
texts.asv: I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for those whom thou hast given me; for they are thine:

texts.webp: All things that are mine are yours, and yours are mine, and I am glorified in them.
texts.bsb: All I have is Yours, and all You have is Mine; and in them I have been glorified.
texts.asv: and all things that are mine are thine, and thine are mine: and I am glorified in them.

texts.webp: I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them through your name which you have given me, that they may be one, even as we are.
texts.bsb: I will no longer be in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to You.
texts.asv: And I am no more in the world, and these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep them in thy name which thou hast given me, that they may be one, even as we are.

texts.webp: While I was with them in the world, I kept them in your name. I have kept those whom you have given me. None of them is lost except the son of destruction, that the Scripture might be fulfilled.
texts.bsb: While I was with them, I protected and preserved them by Your name, the name You gave Me. Not one of them has been lost, except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture would be fulfilled.
texts.asv: While I was with them, I kept them in thy name which thou hast given me: and I guarded them, and not one of them perished, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled.

texts.webp: But now I come to you, and I say these things in the world, that they may have my joy made full in themselves.
texts.bsb: But now I am coming to You; and I am saying these things while I am in the world, so that they may have My joy fulfilled within them.
texts.asv: But now I come to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they may have my joy made full in themselves.

texts.webp: I have given them your word. The world hated them because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
texts.bsb: I have given them Your word and the world has hated them. For they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
texts.asv: I have given them thy word; and the world hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.

texts.webp: I pray not that you would take them from the world, but that you would keep them from the evil one.
texts.bsb: I am not asking that You take them out of the world, but that You keep them from the evil one.
texts.asv: I pray not that thou shouldest take them from the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil one.

texts.webp: They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
texts.bsb: They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
texts.asv: They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.

texts.webp: Sanctify them in your truth. Your word is truth.
texts.bsb: Sanctify them by the truth; Your word is truth.
texts.asv: Sanctify them in the truth: thy word is truth.

texts.webp: As you sent me into the world, even so I have sent them into the world.
texts.bsb: As You sent Me into the world, I have also sent them into the world.
texts.asv: As thou didst send me into the world, even so sent I them into the world.

texts.webp: For their sakes I sanctify myself, that they themselves also may be sanctified in truth.
texts.bsb: For them I sanctify Myself, so that they too may be sanctified by the truth.
texts.asv: And for their sakes I sanctify myself, that they themselves also may be sanctified in truth.

texts.webp: “Not for these only do I pray, but for those also who will believe in me through their word,
texts.bsb: I am not asking on behalf of them alone, but also on behalf of those who will believe in Me through their message,
texts.asv: Neither for these only do I pray, but for them also that believe on me through their word;

texts.webp: that they may all be one; even as you, Father, are in me, and I in you, that they also may be one in us; that the world may believe that you sent me.
texts.bsb: that all of them may be one, as You, Father, are in Me, and I am in You. May they also be in Us, so that the world may believe that You sent Me.
texts.asv: that they may all be one; even as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be in us: that the world may believe that thou didst send me.

texts.webp: The glory which you have given me, I have given to them, that they may be one, even as we are one,
texts.bsb: I have given them the glory You gave Me, so that they may be one as We are one —
texts.asv: And the glory which thou hast given me I have given unto them; that they may be one, even as we are one;

texts.webp: I in them, and you in me, that they may be perfected into one, that the world may know that you sent me and loved them, even as you loved me.
texts.bsb: I in them and You in Me — that they may be perfectly united, so that the world may know that You sent Me and have loved them just as You have loved Me.
texts.asv: I in them, and thou in me, that they may be perfected into one; that the world may know that thou didst send me, and lovedst them, even as thou lovedst me.

texts.webp: Father, I desire that they also whom you have given me be with me where I am, that they may see my glory which you have given me, for you loved me before the foundation of the world.
texts.bsb: Father, I want those You have given Me to be with Me where I am, that they may see the glory You gave Me because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.
texts.asv: Father, I desire that they also whom thou hast given me be with me where I am, that they may behold my glory, which thou hast given me: for thou lovedst me before the foundation of the world.

texts.webp: Righteous Father, the world hasn’t known you, but I knew you; and these knew that you sent me.
texts.bsb: Righteous Father, although the world has not known You, I know You, and they know that You sent Me.
texts.asv: O righteous Father, the world knew thee not, but I knew thee; and these knew that thou didst send me;

texts.webp: I made known to them your name, and will make it known; that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I in them.”
texts.bsb: And I have made Your name known to them and will continue to make it known, so that the love You have for Me may be in them, and I in them.”
texts.asv: and I made known unto them thy name, and will make it known; that the love wherewith thou lovedst me may be in them, and I in them.

texts.webp: When Jesus had spoken these words, he went out with his disciples over the brook Kidron, where there was a garden, into which he and his disciples entered.
texts.bsb: After Jesus had spoken these words, He went out with His disciples across the Kidron Valley, where they entered a garden.
texts.asv: When Jesus had spoken these words, he went forth with his disciples over the brook Kidron, where was a garden, into which he entered, himself and his disciples.

texts.webp: Now Judas, who betrayed him, also knew the place, for Jesus often met there with his disciples.
texts.bsb: Now Judas His betrayer also knew the place, because Jesus had often met there with His disciples.
texts.asv: Now Judas also, who betrayed him, knew the place: for Jesus oft-times resorted thither with his disciples.

texts.webp: Judas then, having taken a detachment of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, came there with lanterns, torches, and weapons.
texts.bsb: So Judas brought a band of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees. They arrived at the garden carrying lanterns, torches, and weapons.
texts.asv: Judas then, having received the band of soldiers, and officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, cometh thither with lanterns and torches and weapons.

texts.webp: Jesus therefore, knowing all the things that were happening to him, went out and said to them, “Who are you looking for?”
texts.bsb: Jesus, knowing all that was coming upon Him, stepped forward and asked them, “Whom are you seeking?”
texts.asv: Jesus therefore, knowing all the things that were coming upon him, went forth, and saith unto them, Whom seek ye?

texts.webp: They answered him, “Jesus of Nazareth.”
texts.bsb: “Jesus of Nazareth,” they answered.
texts.asv: They answered him, Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus saith unto them, I am he. And Judas also, who betrayed him, was standing with them.

texts.webp: When therefore he said to them, “I am he,” they went backward and fell to the ground.
texts.bsb: When Jesus said, “I am He,” they drew back and fell to the ground.
texts.asv: When therefore he said unto them, I am he, they went backward, and fell to the ground.

texts.webp: Again therefore he asked them, “Who are you looking for?”
texts.bsb: So He asked them again, “Whom are you seeking?”
texts.asv: Again therefore he asked them, Whom seek ye? And they said, Jesus of Nazareth.

texts.webp: Jesus answered, “I told you that I am he. If therefore you seek me, let these go their way,”
texts.bsb: “I told you that I am He,” Jesus replied. “So if you are looking for Me, let these men go.”
texts.asv: Jesus answered, I told you that I am he; if therefore ye seek me, let these go their way:

texts.webp: that the word might be fulfilled which he spoke, “Of those whom you have given me, I have lost none.”
texts.bsb: This was to fulfill the word He had spoken: “I have not lost one of those You have given Me.”
texts.asv: that the word might be fulfilled which he spake, Of those whom thou hast given me I lost not one.

texts.webp: Simon Peter therefore, having a sword, drew it, struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus.
texts.bsb: Then Simon Peter drew his sword and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus.
texts.asv: Simon Peter therefore having a sword drew it, and struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his right ear. Now the servant’s name was Malchus.

texts.webp: Jesus therefore said to Peter, “Put the sword into its sheath. The cup which the Father has given me, shall I not surely drink it?”
texts.bsb: “Put your sword back in its sheath!” Jesus said to Peter. “Shall I not drink the cup the Father has given Me?”
texts.asv: Jesus therefore said unto Peter, Put up the sword into the sheath: the cup which the Father hath given me, shall I not drink it?

texts.webp: So the detachment, the commanding officer, and the officers of the Jews seized Jesus and bound him,
texts.bsb: Then the band of soldiers, with its commander and the officers of the Jews, arrested Jesus and bound Him.
texts.asv: So the band and the chief captain, and the officers of the Jews, seized Jesus and bound him,

texts.webp: and led him to Annas first, for he was father-in-law to Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
texts.bsb: They brought Him first to Annas, who was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year.
texts.asv: and led him to Annas first; for he was father in law to Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.

texts.webp: Now it was Caiaphas who advised the Jews that it was expedient that one man should perish for the people.
texts.bsb: Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jews that it would be better if one man died for the people.
texts.asv: Now Caiaphas was he that gave counsel to the Jews, that it was expedient that one man should die for the people.

texts.webp: Simon Peter followed Jesus, as did another disciple. Now that disciple was known to the high priest, and entered in with Jesus into the court of the high priest;
texts.bsb: Now Simon Peter and another disciple were following Jesus. Since that disciple was known to the high priest, he also went with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest.
texts.asv: And Simon Peter followed Jesus, and so did another disciple. Now that disciple was known unto the high priest, and entered in with Jesus into the court of the high priest;

texts.webp: but Peter was standing at the door outside. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to her who kept the door, and brought in Peter.
texts.bsb: But Peter stood outside at the door. Then the disciple who was known to the high priest went out and spoke to the doorkeeper, and brought Peter in.
texts.asv: but Peter was standing at the door without. So the other disciple, who was known unto the high priest, went out and spake unto her that kept the door, and brought in Peter.

texts.webp: Then the maid who kept the door said to Peter, “Are you also one of this man’s disciples?”
texts.bsb: At this, the servant girl watching the door said to Peter, “Aren’t you also one of this man’s disciples?”
texts.asv: The maid therefore that kept the door saith unto Peter, Art thou also one of this man’s disciples? He saith, I am not.

texts.webp: Now the servants and the officers were standing there, having made a fire of coals, for it was cold. They were warming themselves. Peter was with them, standing and warming himself.
texts.bsb: Because it was cold, the servants and officers were standing around a charcoal fire they had made to keep warm. And Peter was also standing with them, warming himself.
texts.asv: Now the servants and the officers were standing there, having made a fire of coals; for it was cold; and they were warming themselves: and Peter also was with them, standing and warming himself.

texts.webp: The high priest therefore asked Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching.
texts.bsb: Meanwhile, the high priest questioned Jesus about His disciples and His teaching.
texts.asv: The high priest therefore asked Jesus of his disciples, and of his teaching.

texts.webp: Jesus answered him, “I spoke openly to the world. I always taught in synagogues and in the temple, where the Jews always meet. I said nothing in secret.
texts.bsb: “I have spoken openly to the world,” Jesus answered. “I always taught in the synagogues and at the temple, where all the Jews come together. I said nothing in secret.
texts.asv: Jesus answered him, I have spoken openly to the world; I ever taught in synagogues, and in the temple, where all the Jews come together; and in secret spake I nothing.

texts.webp: Why do you ask me? Ask those who have heard me what I said to them. Behold, they know the things which I said.”
texts.bsb: Why are you asking Me? Ask those who heard My message. Surely they know what I said.”
texts.asv: Why askest thou me? ask them that have heard me, what I spake unto them: behold, these know the things which I said.

texts.webp: When he had said this, one of the officers standing by slapped Jesus with his hand, saying, “Do you answer the high priest like that?”
texts.bsb: When Jesus had said this, one of the officers standing nearby slapped Him in the face and said, “Is this how You answer the high priest?”
texts.asv: And when he had said this, one of the officers standing by struck Jesus with his hand, saying, Answerest thou the high priest so?

texts.webp: Jesus answered him, “If I have spoken evil, testify of the evil; but if well, why do you beat me?”
texts.bsb: Jesus replied, “If I said something wrong, testify as to what was wrong. But if I spoke correctly, why did you strike Me?”
texts.asv: Jesus answered him, If I have spoken evil, bear witness of the evil: but if well, why smitest thou me?

texts.webp: Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas, the high priest.
texts.bsb: Then Annas sent Him, still bound, to Caiaphas the high priest.
texts.asv: Annas therefore sent him bound unto Caiaphas the high priest.

texts.webp: Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. They said therefore to him, “You aren’t also one of his disciples, are you?”
texts.bsb: Simon Peter was still standing and warming himself. So they asked him, “Aren’t you also one of His disciples?”
texts.asv: Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. They said therefore unto him, Art thou also one of his disciples? He denied, and said, I am not.

texts.webp: One of the servants of the high priest, being a relative of him whose ear Peter had cut off, said, “Didn’t I see you in the garden with him?”
texts.bsb: One of the high priest’s servants, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, asked, “Didn’t I see you with Him in the garden?”
texts.asv: One of the servants of the high priest, being a kinsman of him whose ear Peter cut off, saith, Did not I see thee in the garden with him?

texts.webp: Peter therefore denied it again, and immediately the rooster crowed.
texts.bsb: Peter denied it once more, and immediately a rooster crowed.
texts.asv: Peter therefore denied again: and straightway the cock crew.

texts.webp: They led Jesus therefore from Caiaphas into the Praetorium. It was early, and they themselves didn’t enter into the Praetorium, that they might not be defiled, but might eat the Passover.
texts.bsb: Then they led Jesus away from Caiaphas into the Praetorium. By now it was early morning, and the Jews did not enter the Praetorium, to avoid being defiled and unable to eat the Passover.
texts.asv: They lead Jesus therefore from Caiaphas into the Prætorium: and it was early; and they themselves entered not into the Prætorium, that they might not be defiled, but might eat the passover.

texts.webp: Pilate therefore went out to them and said, “What accusation do you bring against this man?”
texts.bsb: So Pilate went out to them and asked, “What accusation are you bringing against this man?”
texts.asv: Pilate therefore went out unto them, and saith, What accusation bring ye against this man?

texts.webp: They answered him, “If this man weren’t an evildoer, we wouldn’t have delivered him up to you.”
texts.bsb: “If He were not a criminal,” they replied, “we would not have handed Him over to you.”
texts.asv: They answered and said unto him, If this man were not an evil-doer, we should not have delivered him up unto thee.

texts.webp: Pilate therefore said to them, “Take him yourselves, and judge him according to your law.”
texts.bsb: “You take Him and judge Him by your own law,” Pilate told them.
texts.asv: Pilate therefore said unto them, Take him yourselves, and judge him according to your law. The Jews said unto him, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death:

texts.webp: that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spoke, signifying by what kind of death he should die.
texts.bsb: This was to fulfill the word that Jesus had spoken to indicate the kind of death He was going to die.
texts.asv: that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he spake, signifying by what manner of death he should die.

texts.webp: Pilate therefore entered again into the Praetorium, called Jesus, and said to him, “Are you the King of the Jews?”
texts.bsb: Pilate went back into the Praetorium, summoned Jesus, and asked Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?”
texts.asv: Pilate therefore entered again into the Prætorium, and called Jesus, and said unto him, Art thou the King of the Jews?

texts.webp: Jesus answered him, “Do you say this by yourself, or did others tell you about me?”
texts.bsb: “Are you saying this on your own,” Jesus asked, “or did others tell you about Me?”
texts.asv: Jesus answered, Sayest thou this of thyself, or did others tell it thee concerning me?

texts.webp: Pilate answered, “I’m not a Jew, am I? Your own nation and the chief priests delivered you to me. What have you done?”
texts.bsb: “Am I a Jew?” Pilate replied. “Your own people and chief priests handed You over to me. What have You done?”
texts.asv: Pilate answered, Am I a Jew? Thine own nation and the chief priests delivered thee unto me: what hast thou done?

texts.webp: Jesus answered, “My Kingdom is not of this world. If my Kingdom were of this world, then my servants would fight, that I wouldn’t be delivered to the Jews. But now my Kingdom is not from here.”
texts.bsb: Jesus answered, “My kingdom is not of this world; if it were, My servants would fight to prevent My arrest by the Jews. But now My kingdom is not of this realm.”
texts.asv: Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is my kingdom not from hence.

texts.webp: Pilate therefore said to him, “Are you a king then?”
texts.bsb: “Then You are a king!” Pilate said.
texts.asv: Pilate therefore said unto him, Art thou a king then? Jesus answered, Thou sayest that I am a king. To this end have I been born, and to this end am I come into the world, that I should bear witness unto the truth. Every one that is of the truth heareth my voice.

texts.webp: Pilate said to him, “What is truth?”
texts.bsb: “What is truth?” Pilate asked.
texts.asv: Pilate saith unto him, What is truth?

texts.webp: But you have a custom that I should release someone to you at the Passover. Therefore, do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”
texts.bsb: But it is your custom that I release to you one prisoner at the Passover. So then, do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”
texts.asv: But ye have a custom, that I should release unto you one at the passover: will ye therefore that I release unto you the King of the Jews?

texts.webp: Then they all shouted again, saying, “Not this man, but Barabbas!” Now Barabbas was a robber.
texts.bsb: “Not this man,” they shouted, “but Barabbas!” ( Now Barabbas was an insurrectionist. )
texts.asv: They cried out therefore again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas. Now Barabbas was a robber.

texts.webp: So Pilate then took Jesus and flogged him.
texts.bsb: Then Pilate took Jesus and had Him flogged.
texts.asv: Then Pilate therefore took Jesus, and scourged him.

texts.webp: The soldiers twisted thorns into a crown and put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple garment.
texts.bsb: The soldiers twisted together a crown of thorns, set it on His head, and dressed Him in a purple robe.
texts.asv: And the soldiers platted a crown of thorns, and put it on his head, and arrayed him in a purple garment;

texts.webp: They kept saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and they kept slapping him.
texts.bsb: And they went up to Him again and again, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and slapping Him in the face.
texts.asv: and they came unto him, and said, Hail, King of the Jews! and they struck him with their hands.

texts.webp: Then Pilate went out again, and said to them, “Behold, I bring him out to you, that you may know that I find no basis for a charge against him.”
texts.bsb: Once again Pilate came out and said to the Jews, “Look, I am bringing Him out to you to let you know that I find no basis for a charge against Him.”
texts.asv: And Pilate went out again, and saith unto them, Behold, I bring him out to you, that ye may know that I find no crime in him.

texts.webp: Jesus therefore came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment. Pilate said to them, “Behold, the man!”
texts.bsb: When Jesus came out wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe, Pilate said to them, “Here is the man!”
texts.asv: Jesus therefore came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment. And Pilate saith unto them, Behold, the man!

texts.webp: When therefore the chief priests and the officers saw him, they shouted, saying, “Crucify! Crucify!”
texts.bsb: As soon as the chief priests and officers saw Him, they shouted, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!”
texts.asv: When therefore the chief priests and the officers saw him, they cried out, saying, Crucify him, crucify him! Pilate saith unto them, Take him yourselves, and crucify him: for I find no crime in him.

texts.webp: The Jews answered him, “We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.”
texts.bsb: “We have a law,” answered the Jews, “and according to that law He must die, because He declared Himself to be the Son of God.”
texts.asv: The Jews answered him, We have a law, and by that law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.

texts.webp: When therefore Pilate heard this saying, he was more afraid.
texts.bsb: When Pilate heard this statement, he was even more afraid,
texts.asv: When Pilate therefore heard this saying, he was the more afraid;

texts.webp: He entered into the Praetorium again, and said to Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer.
texts.bsb: and he went back into the Praetorium. “Where are You from?” he asked.
texts.asv: and he entered into the Prætorium again, and saith unto Jesus, Whence art thou? But Jesus gave him no answer.

texts.webp: Pilate therefore said to him, “Aren’t you speaking to me? Don’t you know that I have power to release you and have power to crucify you?”
texts.bsb: So Pilate said to Him, “Do You refuse to speak to me? Do You not know that I have authority to release You and authority to crucify You?”
texts.asv: Pilate therefore saith unto him, Speakest thou not unto me? knowest thou not that I have power to release thee, and have power to crucify thee?

texts.webp: Jesus answered, “You would have no power at all against me, unless it were given to you from above. Therefore he who delivered me to you has greater sin.”
texts.bsb: Jesus answered, “You would have no authority over Me if it were not given to you from above. Therefore the one who handed Me over to you is guilty of greater sin.”
texts.asv: Jesus answered him, Thou wouldest have no power against me, except it were given thee from above: therefore he that delivered me unto thee hath greater sin.

texts.webp: At this, Pilate was seeking to release him, but the Jews cried out, saying, “If you release this man, you aren’t Caesar’s friend! Everyone who makes himself a king speaks against Caesar!”
texts.bsb: From then on, Pilate tried to release Him, but the Jews kept shouting, “If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who declares himself a king is defying Caesar.”
texts.asv: Upon this Pilate sought to release him: but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou release this man, thou art not Cæsar’s friend: every one that maketh himself a king speaketh against Cæsar.

texts.webp: When Pilate therefore heard these words, he brought Jesus out and sat down on the judgment seat at a place called “The Pavement”, but in Hebrew, “Gabbatha.”
texts.bsb: When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus out and sat on the judgment seat at a place called the Stone Pavement, which in Hebrew is Gabbatha.
texts.asv: When Pilate therefore heard these words, he brought Jesus out, and sat down on the judgment-seat at a place called The Pavement, but in Hebrew, Gabbatha.

texts.webp: Now it was the Preparation Day of the Passover, at about the sixth hour. He said to the Jews, “Behold, your King!”
texts.bsb: It was the day of Preparation for the Passover, about the sixth hour. And Pilate said to the Jews, “Here is your King!”
texts.asv: Now it was the Preparation of the passover: it was about the sixth hour. And he saith unto the Jews, Behold, your King!

texts.webp: They cried out, “Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!”
texts.bsb: At this, they shouted, “Away with Him! Away with Him! Crucify Him!”
texts.asv: They therefore cried out, Away with him, away with him, crucify him! Pilate saith unto them, Shall I crucify your King? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Cæsar.

texts.webp: So then he delivered him to them to be crucified. So they took Jesus and led him away.
texts.bsb: Then Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified, and the soldiers took Him away.
texts.asv: Then therefore he delivered him unto them to be crucified.

texts.webp: He went out, bearing his cross, to the place called “The Place of a Skull”, which is called in Hebrew, “Golgotha”,
texts.bsb: Carrying His own cross, He went out to The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
texts.asv: They took Jesus therefore: and he went out, bearing the cross for himself, unto the place called The place of a skull, which is called in Hebrew Golgotha:

texts.webp: where they crucified him, and with him two others, on either side one, and Jesus in the middle.
texts.bsb: There they crucified Him, and with Him two others, one on each side, with Jesus in the middle.
texts.asv: where they crucified him, and with him two others, on either side one, and Jesus in the midst.

texts.webp: Pilate wrote a title also, and put it on the cross. There was written, “JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
texts.bsb: Pilate also had a notice posted on the cross. It read:
texts.asv: And Pilate wrote a title also, and put it on the cross. And there was written, JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS.

texts.webp: Therefore many of the Jews read this title, for the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek.
texts.bsb: Many of the Jews read this sign, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.
texts.asv: This title therefore read many of the Jews, for the place where Jesus was crucified was nigh to the city; and it was written in Hebrew, and in Latin, and in Greek.

texts.webp: The chief priests of the Jews therefore said to Pilate, “Don’t write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but, ‘he said, “I am King of the Jews.”’”
texts.bsb: So the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, “Do not write, ‘The King of the Jews,’ but only that He said, ‘I am the King of the Jews.’ ”
texts.asv: The chief priests of the Jews therefore said to Pilate, Write not, The King of the Jews; but, that he said, I am King of the Jews.

texts.webp: Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.”
texts.bsb: Pilate answered, “What I have written, I have written.”
texts.asv: Pilate answered, What I have written I have written.

texts.webp: Then the soldiers, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also the tunic. Now the tunic was without seam, woven from the top throughout.
texts.bsb: When the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they divided His garments into four parts, one for each soldier, with the tunic remaining. It was seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom.
texts.asv: The soldiers therefore, when they had crucified Jesus, took his garments and made four parts, to every soldier a part; and also the coat: now the coat was without seam, woven from the top throughout.

texts.webp: Then they said to one another, “Let’s not tear it, but cast lots for it to decide whose it will be,” that the Scripture might be fulfilled, which says,
texts.bsb: So they said to one another, “Let us not tear it. Instead, let us cast lots to see who will get it.” This was to fulfill the Scripture:
texts.asv: They said therefore one to another, Let us not rend it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be: that the scripture might be fulfilled, which saith,

texts.webp: But standing by Jesus’ cross were his mother, his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
texts.bsb: Near the cross of Jesus stood His mother and her sister, as well as Mary the wife of Clopas and Mary Magdalene.
texts.asv: These things therefore the soldiers did. But there were standing by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.

texts.webp: Therefore when Jesus saw his mother, and the disciple whom he loved standing there, he said to his mother, “Woman, behold, your son!”
texts.bsb: When Jesus saw His mother and the disciple whom He loved standing nearby, He said to His mother, “Woman, here is your son.”
texts.asv: When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold, thy son!

texts.webp: Then he said to the disciple, “Behold, your mother!” From that hour, the disciple took her to his own home.
texts.bsb: Then He said to the disciple, “Here is your mother.” So from that hour, this disciple took her into his home.
texts.asv: Then saith he to the disciple, Behold, thy mother! And from that hour the disciple took her unto his own home.

texts.webp: After this, Jesus, seeing that all things were now finished, that the Scripture might be fulfilled, said, “I am thirsty!”
texts.bsb: After this, knowing that everything had now been accomplished, and to fulfill the Scripture, Jesus said, “I am thirsty.”
texts.asv: After this Jesus, knowing that all things are now finished, that the scripture might be accomplished, saith, I thirst.

texts.webp: Now a vessel full of vinegar was set there; so they put a sponge full of the vinegar on hyssop, and held it at his mouth.
texts.bsb: A jar of sour wine was sitting there. So they soaked a sponge in the wine, put it on a stalk of hyssop, and lifted it to His mouth.
texts.asv: There was set there a vessel full of vinegar: so they put a sponge full of the vinegar upon hyssop, and brought it to his mouth.

texts.webp: When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, “It is finished!” Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
texts.bsb: When Jesus had received the sour wine, He said, “It is finished.” And bowing His head, He yielded up His spirit.
texts.asv: When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up his spirit.

texts.webp: Therefore the Jews, because it was the Preparation Day, so that the bodies wouldn’t remain on the cross on the Sabbath (for that Sabbath was a special one), asked of Pilate that their legs might be broken and that they might be taken away.
texts.bsb: It was the day of Preparation, and the next day was a High Sabbath. In order that the bodies would not remain on the cross during the Sabbath, the Jews asked Pilate to have the legs broken and the bodies removed.
texts.asv: The Jews therefore, because it was the Preparation, that the bodies should not remain on the cross upon the sabbath (for the day of that sabbath was a high day), asked of Pilate that their legs might be broken, and that they might be taken away.

texts.webp: Therefore the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first and of the other who was crucified with him;
texts.bsb: So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man who had been crucified with Jesus, and those of the other.
texts.asv: The soldiers therefore came, and brake the legs of the first, and of the other that was crucified with him:

texts.webp: but when they came to Jesus and saw that he was already dead, they didn’t break his legs.
texts.bsb: But when they came to Jesus and saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs.
texts.asv: but when they came to Jesus, and saw that he was dead already, they brake not his legs:

texts.webp: However, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
texts.bsb: Instead, one of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear, and immediately blood and water flowed out.
texts.asv: howbeit one of the soldiers with a spear pierced his side, and straightway there came out blood and water.

texts.webp: He who has seen has testified, and his testimony is true. He knows that he tells the truth, that you may believe.
texts.bsb: The one who saw it has testified to this, and his testimony is true. He knows that he is telling the truth, so that you also may believe.
texts.asv: And he that hath seen hath borne witness, and his witness is true: and he knoweth that he saith true, that ye also may believe.

texts.webp: For these things happened that the Scripture might be fulfilled, “A bone of him will not be broken.”
texts.bsb: Now these things happened so that the Scripture would be fulfilled: “Not one of His bones will be broken.”
texts.asv: For these things came to pass, that the scripture might be fulfilled, A bone of him shall not be broken.

texts.webp: Again another Scripture says, “They will look on him whom they pierced.”
texts.bsb: And, as another Scripture says: “They will look on the One they have pierced.”
texts.asv: And again another scripture saith, They shall look on him whom they pierced.

texts.webp: After these things, Joseph of Arimathaea, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, asked of Pilate that he might take away Jesus’ body. Pilate gave him permission. He came therefore and took away his body.
texts.bsb: Afterward, Joseph of Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus (but secretly for fear of the Jews), asked Pilate to let him remove the body of Jesus. Pilate gave him permission, so he came and removed His body.
texts.asv: And after these things Joseph of Arimathæa, being a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, asked of Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus: and Pilate gave him leave. He came therefore, and took away his body.

texts.webp: Nicodemus, who at first came to Jesus by night, also came bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred Roman pounds.
texts.bsb: Nicodemus, who had previously come to Jesus at night, also brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about seventy-five pounds.
texts.asv: And there came also Nicodemus, he who at the first came to him by night, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds.

texts.webp: So they took Jesus’ body, and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as the custom of the Jews is to bury.
texts.bsb: So they took the body of Jesus and wrapped it in linen cloths with the spices, according to the Jewish burial custom.
texts.asv: So they took the body of Jesus, and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, as the custom of the Jews is to bury.

texts.webp: Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden. In the garden was a new tomb in which no man had ever yet been laid.
texts.bsb: Now there was a garden in the place where Jesus was crucified, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid.
texts.asv: Now in the place where he was crucified there was a garden; and in the garden a new tomb wherein was never man yet laid.

texts.webp: Then, because of the Jews’ Preparation Day (for the tomb was near at hand), they laid Jesus there.
texts.bsb: And because it was the Jewish day of Preparation and the tomb was nearby, they placed Jesus there.
texts.asv: There then because of the Jews’ Preparation (for the tomb was nigh at hand) they laid Jesus.

texts.webp: Now on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene went early, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and saw that the stone had been taken away from the tomb.
texts.bsb: Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb and saw that the stone had been removed from the entrance.
texts.asv: Now on the first day of the week cometh Mary Magdalene early, while it was yet dark, unto the tomb, and seeth the stone taken away from the tomb.

texts.webp: Therefore she ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and said to them, “They have taken away the Lord out of the tomb, and we don’t know where they have laid him!”
texts.bsb: So she came running to Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one whom Jesus loved. “They have taken the Lord out of the tomb,” she said, “and we do not know where they have put Him!”
texts.asv: She runneth therefore, and cometh to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and saith unto them, They have taken away the Lord out of the tomb, and we know not where they have laid him.

texts.webp: Therefore Peter and the other disciple went out, and they went toward the tomb.
texts.bsb: Then Peter and the other disciple set out for the tomb.
texts.asv: Peter therefore went forth, and the other disciple, and they went toward the tomb.

texts.webp: They both ran together. The other disciple outran Peter and came to the tomb first.
texts.bsb: The two were running together, but the other disciple outran Peter and reached the tomb first.
texts.asv: And they ran both together: and the other disciple outran Peter, and came first to the tomb;

texts.webp: Stooping and looking in, he saw the linen cloths lying there; yet he didn’t enter in.
texts.bsb: He bent down and looked in at the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go in.
texts.asv: and stooping and looking in, he seeth the linen cloths lying; yet entered he not in.

texts.webp: Then Simon Peter came, following him, and entered into the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying,
texts.bsb: Simon Peter arrived just after him. He entered the tomb and saw the linen cloths lying there.
texts.asv: Simon Peter therefore also cometh, following him, and entered into the tomb; and he beholdeth the linen cloths lying,

texts.webp: and the cloth that had been on his head, not lying with the linen cloths, but rolled up in a place by itself.
texts.bsb: The cloth that had been around Jesus’ head was rolled up, lying separate from the linen cloths.
texts.asv: and the napkin, that was upon his head, not lying with the linen cloths, but rolled up in a place by itself.

texts.webp: So then the other disciple who came first to the tomb also entered in, and he saw and believed.
texts.bsb: Then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb first, also went in. And he saw and believed.
texts.asv: Then entered in therefore the other disciple also, who came first to the tomb, and he saw, and believed.

texts.webp: For as yet they didn’t know the Scripture, that he must rise from the dead.
texts.bsb: For they still did not understand from the Scripture that Jesus had to rise from the dead.
texts.asv: For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise again from the dead.

texts.webp: So the disciples went away again to their own homes.
texts.bsb: Then the disciples returned to their homes.
texts.asv: So the disciples went away again unto their own home.

texts.webp: But Mary was standing outside at the tomb weeping. So as she wept, she stooped and looked into the tomb,
texts.bsb: But Mary stood outside the tomb weeping. And as she wept, she bent down to look into the tomb,
texts.asv: But Mary was standing without at the tomb weeping: so, as she wept, she stooped and looked into the tomb;

texts.webp: and she saw two angels in white sitting, one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.
texts.bsb: and she saw two angels in white sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, one at the head and the other at the feet.
texts.asv: and she beholdeth two angels in white sitting, one at the head, and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.

texts.webp: They asked her, “Woman, why are you weeping?”
texts.bsb: “Woman, why are you weeping?” they asked.
texts.asv: And they say unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? She saith unto them, Because they have taken away my Lord, and I know not where they have laid him.

texts.webp: When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing, and didn’t know that it was Jesus.
texts.bsb: When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there. But she did not recognize that it was Jesus.
texts.asv: When she had thus said, she turned herself back, and beholdeth Jesus standing, and knew not that it was Jesus.

texts.webp: Jesus said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping? Who are you looking for?”
texts.bsb: “Woman, why are you weeping?” Jesus asked. “Whom are you seeking?”
texts.asv: Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou hast borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away.

texts.webp: Jesus said to her, “Mary.”
texts.bsb: Jesus said to her, “Mary.”
texts.asv: Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turneth herself, and saith unto him in Hebrew, Rabboni; which is to say, Teacher.

texts.webp: Jesus said to her, “Don’t hold me, for I haven’t yet ascended to my Father; but go to my brothers and tell them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’”
texts.bsb: “Do not cling to Me,” Jesus said, “for I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go and tell My brothers, ‘I am ascending to My Father and your Father, to My God and your God.’”
texts.asv: Jesus saith to her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended unto the Father: but go unto my brethren, and say to them, I ascend unto my Father and your Father, and my God and your God.

texts.webp: Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord, and that he had said these things to her.
texts.bsb: Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, “I have seen the Lord!” And she told them what He had said to her.
texts.asv: Mary Magdalene cometh and telleth the disciples, I have seen the Lord; and that he had said these things unto her.

texts.webp: When therefore it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were locked where the disciples were assembled, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the middle and said to them, “Peace be to you.”
texts.bsb: It was the first day of the week, and that very evening, while the disciples were together with the doors locked for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood among them. “Peace be with you!” He said to them.
texts.asv: When therefore it was evening, on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were shut where the disciples were, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you.

texts.webp: When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side. The disciples therefore were glad when they saw the Lord.
texts.bsb: After He had said this, He showed them His hands and His side.
texts.asv: And when he had said this, he showed unto them his hands and his side. The disciples therefore were glad, when they saw the Lord.

texts.webp: Jesus therefore said to them again, “Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.”
texts.bsb: Again Jesus said to them, “Peace be with you. As the Father has sent Me, so also I am sending you.”
texts.asv: Jesus therefore said to them again, Peace be unto you: as the Father hath sent me, even so send I you.

texts.webp: When he had said this, he breathed on them, and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit!
texts.bsb: When He had said this, He breathed on them and said, “Receive the Holy Spirit.
texts.asv: And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Spirit:

texts.webp: If you forgive anyone’s sins, they have been forgiven them. If you retain anyone’s sins, they have been retained.”
texts.bsb: If you forgive anyone his sins, they are forgiven; if you withhold forgiveness from anyone, it is withheld.”
texts.asv: whose soever sins ye forgive, they are forgiven unto them; whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained.

texts.webp: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, wasn’t with them when Jesus came.
texts.bsb: Now Thomas called Didymus, one of the Twelve, was not with the disciples when Jesus came.
texts.asv: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.

texts.webp: The other disciples therefore said to him, “We have seen the Lord!”
texts.bsb: So the other disciples told him, “We have seen the Lord!”
texts.asv: The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.

texts.webp: After eight days, again his disciples were inside and Thomas was with them. Jesus came, the doors being locked, and stood in the middle, and said, “Peace be to you.”
texts.bsb: Eight days later, His disciples were once again inside with the doors locked, and Thomas was with them. Jesus came and stood among them and said, “Peace be with you.”
texts.asv: And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them. Jesus cometh, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you.

texts.webp: Then he said to Thomas, “Reach here your finger, and see my hands. Reach here your hand, and put it into my side. Don’t be unbelieving, but believing.”
texts.bsb: Then Jesus said to Thomas, “Put your finger here and look at My hands. Reach out your hand and put it into My side. Stop doubting and believe.”
texts.asv: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and see my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and put it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.

texts.webp: Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!”
texts.bsb: Thomas replied, “My Lord and my God!”
texts.asv: Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God.

texts.webp: Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed.”
texts.bsb: Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen Me, you have believed; blessed are those who have not seen and yet have believed.”
texts.asv: Jesus saith unto him, Because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.

texts.webp: Therefore Jesus did many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book;
texts.bsb: Jesus performed many other signs in the presence of His disciples, which are not written in this book.
texts.asv: Many other signs therefore did Jesus in the presence of the disciples, which are not written in this book:

texts.webp: but these are written that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in his name.
texts.bsb: But these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in His name.
texts.asv: but these are written, that ye may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye may have life in his name.

texts.webp: After these things, Jesus revealed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias. He revealed himself this way.
texts.bsb: Later, by the Sea of Tiberias, Jesus again revealed Himself to the disciples. He made Himself known in this way:
texts.asv: After these things Jesus manifested himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and he manifested himself on this wise.

texts.webp: Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples were together.
texts.bsb: Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two other disciples were together.
texts.asv: There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples.

texts.webp: Simon Peter said to them, “I’m going fishing.”
texts.bsb: Simon Peter told them, “I am going fishing.”
texts.asv: Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also come with thee. They went forth, and entered into the boat; and that night they took nothing.

texts.webp: But when day had already come, Jesus stood on the beach; yet the disciples didn’t know that it was Jesus.
texts.bsb: Early in the morning, Jesus stood on the shore, but the disciples did not recognize that it was Jesus.
texts.asv: But when day was now breaking, Jesus stood on the beach: yet the disciples knew not that it was Jesus.

texts.webp: Jesus therefore said to them, “Children, have you anything to eat?”
texts.bsb: So He called out to them, “Children, do you have any fish?”
texts.asv: Jesus therefore saith unto them, Children, have ye aught to eat? They answered him, No.

texts.webp: He said to them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.”
texts.bsb: He told them, “Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” So they cast it there, and they were unable to haul it in because of the great number of fish.
texts.asv: And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes.

texts.webp: That disciple therefore whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It’s the Lord!”
texts.bsb: Then the disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is the Lord!” As soon as Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he put on his outer garment (for he had removed it . . . ) and jumped into the sea.
texts.asv: That disciple therefore whom Jesus loved saith unto Peter, It is the Lord. So when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girt his coat about him (for he was naked), and cast himself into the sea.

texts.webp: But the other disciples came in the little boat (for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits away), dragging the net full of fish.
texts.bsb: The other disciples came ashore in the boat. They dragged in the net full of fish, for they were not far from land, only about a hundred yards.
texts.asv: But the other disciples came in the little boat (for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits off), dragging the net full of fishes.

texts.webp: So when they got out on the land, they saw a fire of coals there, with fish and bread laid on it.
texts.bsb: When they landed, they saw a charcoal fire there with fish on it, and some bread.
texts.asv: So when they got out upon the land, they see a fire of coals there, and fish laid thereon, and bread.

texts.webp: Jesus said to them, “Bring some of the fish which you have just caught.”
texts.bsb: Jesus told them, “Bring some of the fish you have just caught.”
texts.asv: Jesus saith unto them, Bring of the fish which ye have now taken.

texts.webp: Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land, full of one hundred fifty-three great fish. Even though there were so many, the net wasn’t torn.
texts.bsb: So Simon Peter went aboard and dragged the net ashore. It was full of large fish, 153, but even with so many, the net was not torn.
texts.asv: Simon Peter therefore went up, and drew the net to land, full of great fishes, a hundred and fifty and three: and for all there were so many, the net was not rent.

texts.webp: Jesus said to them, “Come and eat breakfast!”
texts.bsb: “Come, have breakfast,” Jesus said to them. None of the disciples dared to ask Him, “Who are You?” They knew it was the Lord.
texts.asv: Jesus saith unto them, Come and break your fast. And none of the disciples durst inquire of him, Who art thou? knowing that it was the Lord.

texts.webp: Then Jesus came and took the bread, gave it to them, and the fish likewise.
texts.bsb: Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and He did the same with the fish.
texts.asv: Jesus cometh, and taketh the bread, and giveth them, and the fish likewise.

texts.webp: This is now the third time that Jesus was revealed to his disciples after he had risen from the dead.
texts.bsb: This was now the third time that Jesus appeared to the disciples after He was raised from the dead.
texts.asv: This is now the third time that Jesus was manifested to the disciples, after that he was risen from the dead.

texts.webp: So when they had eaten their breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these?”
texts.bsb: When they had finished eating, Jesus asked Simon Peter, “Simon son of John, do you love Me more than these?”
texts.asv: So when they had broken their fast, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of John, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.

texts.webp: He said to him again a second time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?”
texts.bsb: Jesus asked a second time, “Simon son of John, do you love Me?”
texts.asv: He saith to him again a second time, Simon, son of John, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Tend my sheep.

texts.webp: He said to him the third time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you have affection for me?”
texts.bsb: Jesus asked a third time, “Simon son of John, do you love Me?”
texts.asv: He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of John, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep.

texts.webp: Most certainly I tell you, when you were young, you dressed yourself and walked where you wanted to. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will dress you and carry you where you don’t want to go.”
texts.bsb: Truly, truly, I tell you, when you were young, you dressed yourself and walked where you wanted; but when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and lead you where you do not want to go.”
texts.asv: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not.

texts.webp: Now he said this, signifying by what kind of death he would glorify God. When he had said this, he said to him, “Follow me.”
texts.bsb: Jesus said this to indicate the kind of death by which Peter would glorify God.
texts.asv: Now this he spake, signifying by what manner of death he should glorify God. And when he had spoken this, he saith unto him, Follow me.

texts.webp: Then Peter, turning around, saw a disciple following. This was the disciple whom Jesus loved, the one who had also leaned on Jesus’ chest at the supper and asked, “Lord, who is going to betray you?”
texts.bsb: Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them. He was the one who had leaned back against Jesus at the supper to ask, “Lord, who is going to betray You?”
texts.asv: Peter, turning about, seeth the disciple whom Jesus loved following; who also leaned back on his breast at the supper, and said, Lord, who is he that betrayeth thee?

texts.webp: Peter, seeing him, said to Jesus, “Lord, what about this man?”
texts.bsb: When Peter saw him, he asked, “Lord, what about him?”
texts.asv: Peter therefore seeing him saith to Jesus, Lord, and what shall this man do?

texts.webp: Jesus said to him, “If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.”
texts.bsb: Jesus answered, “If I want him to remain until I return, what is that to you? You follow Me!”
texts.asv: Jesus saith unto him, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me.

texts.webp: This saying therefore went out among the brothers that this disciple wouldn’t die. Yet Jesus didn’t say to him that he wouldn’t die, but, “If I desire that he stay until I come, what is that to you?”
texts.bsb: Because of this, the rumor spread among the brothers that this disciple would not die. However, Jesus did not say that he would not die, but only, “If I want him to remain until I return, what is that to you?”
texts.asv: This saying therefore went forth among the brethren, that that disciple should not die: yet Jesus said not unto him, that he should not die; but, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee?

texts.webp: This is the disciple who testifies about these things, and wrote these things. We know that his witness is true.
texts.bsb: This is the disciple who testifies to these things and who has written them down. And we know that his testimony is true.
texts.asv: This is the disciple that beareth witness of these things, and wrote these things: and we know that his witness is true.

texts.webp: There are also many other things which Jesus did, which if they would all be written, I suppose that even the world itself wouldn’t have room for the books that would be written.
texts.bsb: There are many more things that Jesus did. If all of them were written down, I suppose that not even the world itself would have space for the books that would be written.
texts.asv: And there are also many other things which Jesus did, the which if they should be written every one, I suppose that even the world itself would not contain the books that should be written.
